# Goal `risk-policies` (Risk-based Conditional Access): findings

Mirror for every Learn path below: `entra-docs-mirror`. Line numbers are file lines (front matter included).
Short names used below:
- CRP = `docs/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies (ms.date 2025-10-30)
- CIP = `docs/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies (2026-05-15)
- RU = `docs/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock (2026-05-15)
- DEP = `docs/id-protection/how-to-deploy-identity-protection.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/how-to-deploy-identity-protection (2025-08-06)
- FAQ = `docs/id-protection/id-protection-faq.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/id-protection-faq (2026-03-17)
- PRU = `docs/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-user.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-user (2026-03-24)
- PRS = `docs/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-sign-in.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-sign-in (2026-03-24)
- MGD = `docs/identity/conditional-access/managed-policies.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/managed-policies (2026-05-28)
- GRANT = `docs/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-grant.md`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-grant

All of these URLs resolve with HTTP 200 and no redirect.

## Headline findings

1. **MT.1013 and CIS.M365.5.2.2.6 fail a tenant that follows Learn today.** Learn now recommends the **Require risk
   remediation** grant for high user risk (CRP L84-91, PRU L63-86). It covers password and passwordless users. Both
   tests require `passwordChange` and reject `riskRemediation`. Graph also returns `riskRemediation` as
   `unknownFutureValue` unless the request sends `Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members`
   (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccessgrantcontrols, builtInControls row).
   `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy` sends no such header. Do not tag MT.1013 until it accepts risk remediation.
2. **CISA.MS.AAD.2.1 (block high-risk users) is a different step, and it conflicts with self-remediation.**
   CIP L85 and MGD L207: when a user is in more than one risk policy, Block overrides the other controls.
   Learn says to put each user in only one of these policies.
3. **Password writeback applies to the user-risk policy only, not to sign-in risk.** Sign-in risk is cleared by
   MFA (CRP L95-97, RU L84). Writeback stays `Unchecked`: `passwordWritebackEnabled` on
   `onPremisesDirectorySynchronizationFeature` is documented as "isn't in use"
   (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/onpremisesdirectorysynchronizationfeature).
4. **The goal needs one anchor step, and the draft's last step (`entra.ca-risk-policies-separate`) is not one.**
   See "Goal anchor" at the end.
5. "Remediate existing risky users first" **is** in Learn: CRP L103 and DEP L75-83 (step 1 of the deployment plan).
6. "Separate policies" **is** in Learn: a warning at the top of CRP (L50-52).

## Steps, in order

### 1. `entra.mfa-registered` (state; another session writes its check; keep Unchecked here)
Title: "Enabled member users are registered for MFA". The relationship is confirmed: **Requires** from
`entra.ca-user-risk` and `entra.ca-sign-in-risk`. It is not required by the block steps. Sources:
- CRP L74-76: users must register for MFA before they need to remediate. Users who aren't registered are blocked
  until an admin steps in. Note: *"A user who isn't registered for MFA when risk is detected can't self-remediate
  and stays blocked until an admin acts. Get users registered before either risk policy is on."*
- PRS L52: an unregistered user can't register for MFA during a risky session, so the risky sign-in is blocked
  (AADSTS53004). Note: *"Users can't register MFA in a risky session, so a risky sign-in by an unregistered user is
  blocked with AADSTS53004."*
- Supporting: CIP L105-107, GRANT L246-250, DEP L98-100. MGD L193: Microsoft scopes its own managed remediation
  policy to users who are registered for MFA.
- For the mfa-registered session: the ID Protection MFA registration policy
  (`docs/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy.md` L57-69, 14-day grace) and DEP L112-114.
  The ZTA check for it is ZTA.21893, "Enable Microsoft Entra ID Protection policy to enforce multifactor
  authentication registration".

### 2. `entra.password-hash-sync` (OnlyWhen `hybrid-identity`)
Title "Turn on password hash synchronization". Summary: "Microsoft Entra ID holds hashes of synced users'
passwords, so leaked credentials can be matched to them." **RecommendedFirst** for `entra.ca-user-risk`. It is not
Requires: the policy works without it, but it misses leaked-credential risk for synced users.
- FAQ L67-69, L96-98, L104-108; `docs/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks.md` L300-306
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks); and
  `docs/identity/hybrid/connect/whatis-phs.md` L57-61 (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/whatis-phs).
  These say the leaked-credentials detection needs PHS for on-premises passwords, that it always sets user risk to
  high, and that only leaks found after PHS is on are checked.
  Note: *"Leaked-credential detection sets user risk to high and needs password hash sync for synced users. Only
  leaks found after it is on are matched, so turn it on early."*
- Also: RU L105 and L248-250 (PHS must be on before an on-premises password change can remediate risk), FAQ
  L145-147, and MGD L197 (Microsoft's managed remediation policy targets hybrid tenants that have PHS).
- Test **CIS.M365.5.1.8.1** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.1.8.1.ps1`). Done when
  `directory/onPremisesSynchronization` `features.passwordSyncEnabled` is true. It skips cloud-only tenants
  (NotApplicable), app-only connections, and federated tenants with PHS off (custom skip, L55-61). **Matches.**
  Because of the federated skip, the step shows Unknown rather than Not done in that case. Learn wants PHS for
  leaked credentials even under federation. Accept this, or have CIS keep its skip and accept the Unknown.

### 3. `entra.password-writeback` (OnlyWhen `hybrid-identity`; Unchecked)
Title "Turn on password writeback". Summary: "Password changes made in Microsoft Entra ID, including risk
remediation, are written back to on-premises AD." **Requires** from `entra.ca-user-risk` only. Remove it from the
sign-in-risk chain, because sign-in risk is cleared by MFA (CRP L95-97, RU L84-87).
- CRP L76: for users synced from on-premises, password writeback must be on. Note: *"For users synced from
  on-premises, Learn makes password writeback a condition of clearing user risk with a secure password change."*
- Effect of risk remediation and passwordless users (the question in the brief): CIP L76-80. Password users get a
  secure password change, so writeback still matters for them. Passwordless users only have their sessions revoked,
  so they don't need it. A hybrid tenant almost always has password users, so keep **Requires**.
- Alternative route: users on domain-joined or hybrid-joined Windows devices can change their password on-premises.
  With PHS and the opt-in setting "Allow on-premises password change to reset user risk", that clears user risk
  (RU L105, L170-175, L248-263; FAQ L147). I don't recommend `RequiresOneOf` now: the route covers only those
  device users, Learn calls it opt-in and asks you to evaluate it (RU L257), and nothing checks it. Later you could
  add `entra.on-premises-password-change-resets-risk` (Unchecked, Requires PHS) and switch to RequiresOneOf.
- Counterpoint: MGD L197 lists only PHS as the eligibility condition for hybrid tenants, not writeback. In practice
  Requires on an Unchecked step only makes `entra.ca-user-risk` Unconfirmed, never Blocked.
- Unchecked text: "Microsoft Graph doesn't report whether password writeback is on."

### 4. `entra.remediate-risky-users`
Title "Remediate existing high-risk users". Summary: "Users that ID Protection already rates high risk are
remediated, dismissed or confirmed safe before policies start acting on them." **RecommendedFirst** for
`entra.ca-user-risk`.
- CRP L101-103: investigate and remediate active risks before enabling the policies. DEP L75-83: reviewing the
  reports is step 1 of the plan. Note: *"Clear the risk already in the ID Protection reports before switching on the
  risk policies. Learn puts this review first in its deployment plan."*
- Test **MT.1260** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1260.ps1` L46-77). Done when v1.0 `identityProtection/riskyUsers`
  has no user with `riskLevel` high and `riskState` atRisk or confirmedCompromised. **Matches**, because the step
  is scoped to high risk. Learn says "any active risks", which is broader, but the user-risk policy acts on high.
- ZTA.21861 "All high-risk users are triaged" checks only atRisk with High, which is narrower. ZTA.21863 "All
  high-risk sign-ins are triaged" checks a different object. It could become a sibling step; I'm not proposing one.

### 5. `entra.ca-user-risk`
Title "Require risk remediation for high user risk in Conditional Access". Summary: "Users that ID Protection rates
high risk must remediate, with a secure password change or a fresh sign-in, before they get access."
Learn's definition of done (PRU L63-86, CRP L84-91 and L114-135, GRANT L258-266):
- an enabled policy that targets All users and All resources, with emergency access accounts excluded;
- the user risk condition includes High;
- the grant is Require risk remediation (authentication strength and sign-in frequency Every time are added
  automatically);
- no sign-in risk condition in the same policy.

Require password change with MFA is the older control and is still documented. CIP L66-72 treats it as
self-remediation too, and L85 says risk remediation takes precedence over it.
- **Requires** `entra.mfa-registered` and `entra.password-writeback` (sources above). Also `entra.emergency-access-excluded`
  (PRU L52-55, CRP L105-110), as in M1.
- **RecommendedFirst** `entra.remediate-risky-users` and `entra.password-hash-sync` (sources above).
- **RecommendedFirst** `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`: PRU L56 recommends excluding service accounts such as the
  Entra Connect Sync account. That is only the general bullet; unlike the compliance page L85, the risk pages have
  no procedure step for it, so RecommendedFirst rather than Requires. Note: *"Learn recommends leaving service
  accounts such as the Entra Connect sync account out of risk policies, as it does for other policies that target
  all users."*
- **Conflicts** `entra.ca-block-high-risk-users` (new step, below). Source: CIP L85 and MGD L207, with FAQ L131-133
  presenting the block as a stopgap until MFA is rolled out. Note: *"A block wins over risk remediation for a user
  in both policies, so that user never self-remediates. Learn says to keep each user in only one of them."*
  This is a decision for you: the path will then tell CISA-aligned tenants to drop the block.
- Licence: Learn says P2 is required (CIP L60-62, PRU L48). Every verifying test already has
  `License = 'AAD_PREMIUM_P2'`, and section 4.2 of the design says steps carry no licence, so add no `OnlyWhen`.
  The consequence is that a tenant without P2 shows Unknown with a NotLicensed reason, not Not applicable. That is
  an engine question.
- Rollout:
  1. "Create the policy in report-only mode and review the impact, including the risk-based policy impact workbook."
     (PRU L83-86; DEP L106-108, L132; FAQ L143)
  2. "Turn it on for a pilot group." (DEP L64-65: a test user and group before real users)
  3. "Turn it on for all users, keeping the emergency access accounts excluded."
  4. "Keep it as its own policy, with no sign-in risk condition." (CRP L50-52)
- Tests:
  - **MT.1013** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1013.ps1` L38-58). Done when an enabled policy has `passwordChange`,
    includeUsers All, includeApplications All and `high` in userRiskLevels. **Narrower**: it rejects
    `riskRemediation`, and it doesn't reject a policy that combines both risk conditions. Fix the test to accept
    risk remediation, then name this step. Its .ps1 Learn link (`howto-conditional-access-policy-risk-user`) is an
    old redirecting URL.
  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.6** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.6.ps1` L41-63). Done when an enabled policy covers all users
    and all apps with no other narrowing condition (so a policy that also has sign-in risk fails), High, passwordChange
    together with MFA or an authentication strength, sign-in frequency Every time, and an AND operator. **Different**:
    it demands password change specifically. Recommend **no step**, or its own step
    `entra.ca-user-risk-password-change` if every CIS test must carry one. Either way it can't share this step.
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.2.1**: blocks. A different setting; see the new step.
  - ZTA.21797 "Restrict access to high risk users" (ZTA 3.1.0 `Test-Assessment.21797.ps1`). Done when an enabled
    policy for high user risk blocks or requires password change, in any scope; when FIDO2 or CBA-MFA is enabled, only
    a block counts. Doesn't match. The ZTA taxonomy has AlsoCheckedBy MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6.
  - MGD L191-205: Microsoft's managed "Require remediation for high-risk users" policy is scoped to a group, so the
    All-users tests fail it. Worth a line in the guide.

### 6. `entra.ca-sign-in-risk`
Title "Require MFA for medium and high sign-in risk in Conditional Access". Summary: "Sign-ins that ID Protection
rates medium or high risk need a fresh MFA, which also clears the sign-in risk."
Learn's definition of done (PRS L68-91, CRP L93-97 and L137-161):
- All users and All resources;
- sign-in risk Medium and High;
- authentication strength Multifactor authentication (Passwordless MFA or Phishing-resistant MFA for passwordless
  users, PRS L93-113);
- sign-in frequency Every time;
- a separate policy.
- **Requires** `entra.mfa-registered` and `entra.emergency-access-excluded` (PRS L56-59).
- **RecommendedFirst** `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts` (PRS L60, same Note as step 5).
- **RecommendedFirst** `entra.trusted-named-locations` (new, optional, below).
- No PHS or writeback edges.
- Rollout: the same three steps as step 5, plus the separate-policy sentence. DEP L118 explicitly says to start
  sign-in risk policies on a subset of users.
- Tests:
  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.7** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.7.ps1` L41-63). Done when an enabled policy covers all
    users and all apps with no other narrowing condition, medium and high, either MFA or an authentication strength
    with Every time, or a block, and an AND operator. **Matches** (it also accepts a block, which is stricter).
    Name this step.
  - **MT.1012** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1012.ps1` L38-62). Done when an enabled policy without passwordChange
    has MFA or a strength whose requirementsSatisfied includes mfa, All users, All apps, and high and medium.
    **Looser**: it doesn't check sign-in frequency Every time (CRP L97, L154-157; PRS L84-87) or the separate
    policy, and it rejects a block. Either add those checks and treat a block as a pass, then name this step, or
    give it no step. Its .ps1 Learn link (`howto-conditional-access-policy-risk`) is an old redirecting URL.
  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.8** (L2, `tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.8.ps1` L41-61). Done when a policy blocks medium and
    high for all users and all apps, with no excluded apps. **Different setting.** No step. Learn rates
    self-remediation above blocking (CRP L70-72).
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.2.3** (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.2.3.ps1` L38-46). Done when an enabled policy blocks high
    sign-in risk for All users and All apps. **Different setting.** No Learn conflict: a block at High plus MFA at
    Medium is coherent (FAQ L141). Recommend no step now. If one is wanted, add a standalone
    `entra.ca-block-high-risk-sign-ins` that Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`.
  - ZTA.21799 "Restrict high risk sign-ins". Done when a policy for high sign-in risk (medium isn't needed) targets
    All users and has block, MFA or a strength. Looser, and its title doesn't match medium and high.
  - MGD L165-176: Microsoft's managed "MFA and reauthentication for risky sign-ins" policy covers only high and may
    be scoped to a group, so it doesn't meet this step.

### 7. `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate`
Title "Keep user risk and sign-in risk in separate policies". Summary: "No Conditional Access policy sets both risk
conditions, so each policy applies when its own risk is detected."
- CRP L50-52 (the warning), plus `docs/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies.md` L59
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies): assignments
  are ANDed. Note: *"Learn warns against setting both risk conditions in one policy. Conditions combine with AND, so
  such a policy applies only when both risks are present."*
- Test **MT.1049** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1049.ps1`, which calls
  `powershell/internal/checks/maester/entra/Test-MtCaMisconfiguredIDProtection.ps1` L29-55). Done when no enabled
  policy has both userRiskLevels and signInRiskLevels; it's skipped when no enabled policy has a risk condition.
  **Matches.** It is not a shim; no other test calls the helper.
- Learn gives no ordering edge for this step. See "Goal anchor".

## New steps proposed

- **`entra.ca-block-high-risk-users`** (CISA.MS.AAD.2.1). Title "Block high-risk users in Conditional Access".
  Summary: "Users that ID Protection rates high risk can't sign in until an admin clears the risk."
  - Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded` (MGD L189).
  - Sources: CIP L70 (block is an option), MGD L180-189 (Microsoft-managed block policy), FAQ L131-133 (a block
    as a mitigation while MFA isn't rolled out). Note: *"A block stops compromised accounts but also legitimate
    users, who then need an admin. Learn suggests it only while users can't yet do MFA."*
  - Test `tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.2.1.ps1` L38-46. Done when an enabled policy blocks high user risk for
    All users and All apps. **Matches.**
  - It sits outside the goal; it is reached only through step 5's Conflicts entry.
- **`entra.trusted-named-locations`** (optional). Title "Mark your known networks as trusted named locations".
  Summary: "ID Protection treats sign-ins from trusted networks as less risky, which cuts false positives."
  - RecommendedFirst for `entra.ca-sign-in-risk`.
  - Sources: CRP L68, and DEP L102-104 (named locations improve the accuracy of risk scores). Note: *"ID Protection
    uses trusted locations in some detections. Marking office and VPN ranges as trusted reduces false positives
    before sign-in risk prompts begin."*
  - Tests: **CIS.M365.5.2.2.14** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.14.ps1` L39-51: at least one IP named location
    that is trusted and has ranges) matches. ZTA.21865 "Named locations are configured" (any `isTrusted` location)
    matches, and its taxonomy has AlsoCheckedBy CIS.M365.5.2.2.14.

## Goal anchor (decision needed)

A goal has one `Step`, but Learn gives two sibling policies and a configuration rule. Options:
- **A (recommended, everything sourced from Learn):** the goal Step is `entra.ca-user-risk`, with `entra.ca-sign-in-risk`
  as its **RecommendedFirst**. RU L89 says sign-in risk left unremediated raises user risk, and a sign-in risk policy
  lets users clear it first. Note: *"With a sign-in risk policy on, users clear risky sign-ins with MFA, so fewer of
  them build up the high user risk that the user-risk policy acts on."*
  `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate` becomes a standalone step for MT.1049, and the rule also appears in both steps'
  Rollout.
- B (closest to the draft): the goal Step is `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate`, which Requires both policy steps.
  Learn doesn't document that ordering, so it needs a `Maintainer` source (section 4.5). MT.1049 passes when only
  one policy exists, so the step's status alone overstates progress.
- C: two goals, `user-risk-policy` and `sign-in-risk-policy`, each anchored on its own policy step.

## Other tests checked (no step)

- CISA.MS.AAD.2.2 reads `identityProtection/settings/notifications` (high-risk user alerts). DEP L126-128 puts it
  after deployment, so it isn't a prerequisite. It is a candidate for a later monitoring step.
- MT.1006, 1007, 1008, 1009, 1011, 1016, CIS 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2, 5.2.2.5, 5.2.2.13 and MT.1195 only exclude
  risk-conditioned policies from their own checks. They don't verify these steps.
- EIDSCA and ORCA: none read risk policies or risky users. EIDSCA.AG02 (report suspicious activity) feeds one
  user-risk detection, but Learn doesn't make it a prerequisite. No EIDSCA or ORCA test verifies these steps.
- No test reads the legacy ID Protection risk policies, which retired on 2026-10-01 (CRP L189-191, CIP L113-115).
  No migration step is needed.
- No shims among any of the tests above.

## Draft changes summary

1. Move `entra.password-writeback` off the sign-in-risk chain; it is Requires for `entra.ca-user-risk` only.
2. Make `entra.password-hash-sync` RecommendedFirst for `entra.ca-user-risk` only.
3. Make `entra.remediate-risky-users` RecommendedFirst for `entra.ca-user-risk`.
4. `entra.ca-user-risk`: MT.1013 is tagged only after it accepts `riskRemediation`. CIS.M365.5.2.2.6 gets no step
   (or its own). CISA.MS.AAD.2.1 moves to the new `entra.ca-block-high-risk-users`.
5. `entra.ca-sign-in-risk`: CIS.M365.5.2.2.7 names it. MT.1012 names it only after it checks sign-in frequency
   Every time. CISA.MS.AAD.2.3 gets no step, or a standalone block step.

- Sign-in risk policy

Warning

Don't combine sign-in risk and user risk conditions in the same Conditional Access policy. Create separate policies for each risk condition.

![Screenshot of a Conditional Access policy showing risk as conditions.](media/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies/sign-in-risk-conditions.png)

## Prerequisites
----
### Risk remediation

Organizations can choose to block access when risk is detected. Blocking sometimes stops legitimate users from doing what they need to. A better solution is to configure user and sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policies that [allow users to self-remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock#end-user-self-remediation).

Warning

Users must register for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication before they face a situation requiring remediation. For hybrid users that are synced from on-premises, password writeback must be enabled. Users not registered are blocked and require administrator intervention.

Password change (I know my password and want to change it to something new) outside of the risky user policy remediation flow doesn't meet the requirement for secure password change.

### Microsoft recommendations

Microsoft recommends the following risk policy configurations to protect your organization:

### User risk policy

Organizations should select **Require risk remediation** when user risk level is **High**. For passwordless users, Microsoft Entra revokes the user's sessions so they must reauthenticate. For users with passwords, they're prompted to complete a secure password change after a successful Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication.

When **Require risk remediation** is selected, two settings are automatically applied:

- **Require authentication strength** is automatically selected as a grant control.
- **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control.

### Sign-in risk policy

Require Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication when sign-in risk level is **Medium** or **High**. This configuration allows users to prove it's them by using one of their registered authentication methods, remediating the sign-in risk.

We also recommend including the [sign-in frequency session control](../identity/conditional-access/concept-session-lifetime#require-reauthentication-every-time) to require reauthentication for risky sign-ins. A successful "strong authentication" usually via multifactor authentication or passwordless authentication, is the only way to self-remediate sign-in risk, regardless of the risk level.

## Enable policies

Organizations can choose to deploy risk-based policies in Conditional Access using the following steps or use [Conditional Access templates](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

Before organizations enable these policies, they should take action to [investigate](howto-identity-protection-investigate-risk) and [remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock) any active risks.

----

Organizations can deploy this policy by following the steps outlined below or by using the [Conditional Access templates](concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

## Require risk remediation

This risk remediation policy covers both password-based and passwordless users.

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access**.
3. Select **New policy**.
4. Give your policy a name. We recommend that organizations create a meaningful standard for the names of their policies.
5. Under **Assignments**, select **Users or workload identities**.
    1. Under **Include**, select **All users**.
    2. Under **Exclude**, select **Users and groups** and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts.
    3. Select **Done**.
6. Under **Target resources** > **Include**, select **All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')**.
7. Under **Conditions** > **User risk**, set **Configure** to **Yes**.
    1. Under **Configure user risk levels needed for policy to be enforced**, select **High**. [This guidance is based on Microsoft recommendations and might be different for each organization](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#choosing-acceptable-risk-levels)
    2. Select **Done**.
8. Under **Access controls** > **Grant**, select **Grant access**.
    1. Select **Require risk remediation**. The **Require authentication strength** grant control is automatically selected. Choose the strength appropriate for your organization.
    2. Select **Select**.
9. Under **Session**, **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control and is mandatory.
10. Confirm your settings and set **Enable policy** to **Report-only**.
11. Select **Create** to create your policy.

After confirming your settings using [policy impact or report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only#reviewing-results), move the **Enable policy** toggle from **Report-only** to **On**.---
## User risk-based Conditional Access policy

ID Protection analyzes signals about user accounts and calculates a risk score based on the probability that the user is compromised. If a user has risky user sign-in behavior, or their credentials were leaked, ID Protection uses these signals to calculate the user risk level. Administrators can configure risk-based Conditional Access policies to enforce access controls based on user risk, including requirements such as:

1. Require risk remediation: ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow for all authentication methods.
2. Require password change: ID Protection blocks access until user completes a secure password change.
3. Block access: ID Protection blocks the user until risk is addressed.

Policies requiring either #1 or #2 forces end users to remediate their user risk and unblock themselves.

## Require risk remediation control

This control uses adaptive risk remediation to let you author a Conditional Access risk policy that accommodates all authentication methods, including password-based and passwordless. This means that when you select "Require risk remediation" in your policy's grant controls, Microsoft Entra ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow based on the threat observed and the user's authentication method. For detailed steps on how to enable adaptive risk remediation, see [Configure risk policies](howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#microsoft-recommendations).

- **Password authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, such as a leaked credential, password spray, or session history involving a compromised password. The user is prompted to perform a secure password change and when completed, their previous sessions are revoked.
- **Passwordless authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, but it doesn't involve a compromised password. Possible risk detections include anomalous token, impossible travel, or unfamiliar sign-in properties. The user's sessions are revoked and they're prompted to sign in again.
- **Attacker-added device**: Risky user is flagged by Microsoft's threat intelligence as having a device added by an attacker. The Entra device object is disabled, blocking new token issuance. The user's sessions are revoked, and they're prompted to sign-in again.

#### Special considerations

- **Require Risk Remediation** remediates user risk, not sign-in risk.
- If a user is assigned to multiple policies, precedence applies: **Require risk remediation** overrides **Require password change**, and **Block** overrides all others. To avoid conflicts, assign each user to only one of these policies at a time.
- **Require authentication strength** and **Sign-in frequency - Every time** are automatically applied to the policy to ensure that after session revocation, end users are immediately prompted to reauthenticate with the specified authentication strength.

    1. Select **Require risk remediation**. The **Require authentication strength** grant control is automatically selected. Choose the strength appropriate for your organization.

## User risk-based Conditional Access policy

ID Protection analyzes signals about user accounts and calculates a risk score based on the probability that the user is compromised. If a user has risky user sign-in behavior, or their credentials were leaked, ID Protection uses these signals to calculate the user risk level. Administrators can configure risk-based Conditional Access policies to enforce access controls based on user risk, including requirements such as:

1. Require risk remediation: ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow for all authentication methods.
2. Require password change: ID Protection blocks access until user completes a secure password change.
3. Block access: ID Protection blocks the user until risk is addressed.

Policies requiring either #1 or #2 forces end users to remediate their user risk and unblock themselves.

## Require risk remediation control

This control uses adaptive risk remediation to let you author a Conditional Access risk policy that accommodates all authentication methods, including password-based and passwordless. This means that when you select "Require risk remediation" in your policy's grant controls, Microsoft Entra ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow based on the threat observed and the user's authentication method. - **Password authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, such as a leaked credential, password spray, or session history involving a compromised password. The user is prompted to perform a secure password change and when completed, their previous sessions are revoked.
- **Passwordless authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, but it doesn't involve a compromised password. Possible risk detections include anomalous token, impossible travel, or unfamiliar sign-in properties. The user's sessions are revoked and they're prompted to sign in again.
- **Attacker-added device**: Risky user is flagged by Microsoft's threat intelligence as having a device added by an attacker. The Entra device object is disabled, blocking new token issuance. The user's sessions are revoked, and they're prompted to sign-in again.

content.content:
- Sign-in risk policy

Warning

Don't combine sign-in risk and user risk conditions in the same Conditional Access policy. Create separate policies for each risk condition.

![Screenshot of a Conditional Access policy showing risk as conditions.](media/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies/sign-in-risk-conditions.png)

## Prerequisites
----
### Risk remediation

Organizations can choose to block access when risk is detected. Blocking sometimes stops legitimate users from doing what they need to. A better solution is to configure user and sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policies that [allow users to self-remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock#end-user-self-remediation).

Warning

Users must register for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication before they face a situation requiring remediation. For hybrid users that are synced from on-premises, password writeback must be enabled. Users not registered are blocked and require administrator intervention.

Password change (I know my password and want to change it to something new) outside of the risky user policy remediation flow doesn't meet the requirement for secure password change.

### Microsoft recommendations

Microsoft recommends the following risk policy configurations to protect your organization:

### User risk policy

Organizations should select **Require risk remediation** when user risk level is **High**. For passwordless users, Microsoft Entra revokes the user's sessions so they must reauthenticate. For users with passwords, they're prompted to complete a secure password change after a successful Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication.

When **Require risk remediation** is selected, two settings are automatically applied:

- **Require authentication strength** is automatically selected as a grant control.
- **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control.

### Sign-in risk policy

Require Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication when sign-in risk level is **Medium** or **High**. This configuration allows users to prove it's them by using one of their registered authentication methods, remediating the sign-in risk.

We also recommend including the [sign-in frequency session control](../identity/conditional-access/concept-session-lifetime#require-reauthentication-every-time) to require reauthentication for risky sign-ins. A successful "strong authentication" usually via multifactor authentication or passwordless authentication, is the only way to self-remediate sign-in risk, regardless of the risk level.

## Enable policies

Organizations can choose to deploy risk-based policies in Conditional Access using the following steps or use [Conditional Access templates](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

Before organizations enable these policies, they should take action to [investigate](howto-identity-protection-investigate-risk) and [remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock) any active risks.

----

Organizations can deploy this policy by following the steps outlined below or by using the [Conditional Access templates](concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

## Require risk remediation

This risk remediation policy covers both password-based and passwordless users.

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access**.
3. Select **New policy**.
4. Give your policy a name. We recommend that organizations create a meaningful standard for the names of their policies.
5. Under **Assignments**, select **Users or workload identities**.
    1. Under **Include**, select **All users**.
    2. Under **Exclude**, select **Users and groups** and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts.
    3. Select **Done**.
6. Under **Target resources** > **Include**, select **All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')**.
7. Under **Conditions** > **User risk**, set **Configure** to **Yes**.
    1. Under **Configure user risk levels needed for policy to be enforced**, select **High**. [This guidance is based on Microsoft recommendations and might be different for each organization](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#choosing-acceptable-risk-levels)
    2. Select **Done**.
8. Under **Access controls** > **Grant**, select **Grant access**.
    1. Select **Require risk remediation**. The **Require authentication strength** grant control is automatically selected. Choose the strength appropriate for your organization.
    2. Select **Select**.
9. Under **Session**, **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control and is mandatory.
10. Confirm your settings and set **Enable policy** to **Report-only**.
11. Select **Create** to create your policy.

After confirming your settings using [policy impact or report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only#reviewing-results), move the **Enable policy** toggle from **Report-only** to **On**.---
## User risk-based Conditional Access policy

ID Protection analyzes signals about user accounts and calculates a risk score based on the probability that the user is compromised. If a user has risky user sign-in behavior, or their credentials were leaked, ID Protection uses these signals to calculate the user risk level. Administrators can configure risk-based Conditional Access policies to enforce access controls based on user risk, including requirements such as:

1. Require risk remediation: ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow for all authentication methods.
2. Require password change: ID Protection blocks access until user completes a secure password change.
3. Block access: ID Protection blocks the user until risk is addressed.

Policies requiring either #1 or #2 forces end users to remediate their user risk and unblock themselves.

## Require risk remediation control

This control uses adaptive risk remediation to let you author a Conditional Access risk policy that accommodates all authentication methods, including password-based and passwordless. This means that when you select "Require risk remediation" in your policy's grant controls, Microsoft Entra ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow based on the threat observed and the user's authentication method. For detailed steps on how to enable adaptive risk remediation, see [Configure risk policies](howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#microsoft-recommendations).

- **Password authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, such as a leaked credential, password spray, or session history involving a compromised password. The user is prompted to perform a secure password change and when completed, their previous sessions are revoked.
- **Passwordless authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, but it doesn't involve a compromised password. Possible risk detections include anomalous token, impossible travel, or unfamiliar sign-in properties. The user's sessions are revoked and they're prompted to sign in again.
- **Attacker-added device**: Risky user is flagged by Microsoft's threat intelligence as having a device added by an attacker. The Entra device object is disabled, blocking new token issuance. The user's sessions are revoked, and they're prompted to sign-in again.

#### Special considerations

- **Require Risk Remediation** remediates user risk, not sign-in risk.
- If a user is assigned to multiple policies, precedence applies: **Require risk remediation** overrides **Require password change**, and **Block** overrides all others. To avoid conflicts, assign each user to only one of these policies at a time.
- **Require authentication strength** and **Sign-in frequency - Every time** are automatically applied to the policy to ensure that after session revocation, end users are immediately prompted to reauthenticate with the specified authentication strength.

2	
3	Mirror paths are relative to `scratchpad/mirrors/`. All `entra-docs-mirror` paths start `entra-docs-mirror/docs/`.
4	ZTA logic was read in the installed module `~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/ZeroTrustAssessment/3.1.0/tests/`;
5	the titles below are the pack catalogue's (2.6.0).
6	
7	## Headline findings
8	
9	1. **MT.1001 is looser than `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`.** It passes on any enabled policy with
10	   `compliantDevice` in the grant, whatever the users, apps or operator (`Test.MT.1001.ps1:41,52`). A "compliant OR
11	   MFA" policy for one app makes the step Done. ZTA.24824 is just as loose. No test checks the Learn policy (all
12	   users, all resources, compliant device only). Either tighten MT.1001 or accept that "Done" means only "the control is in use".
13	2. **The CIS 5.2.2.9 example in section 5 is slightly off.** CIS.M365.5.2.2.9 *requires* `compliantDevice` and only
14	   *allows* `domainJoinedDevice` beside it (`Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.9.ps1:49`), so a policy that requires only hybrid join
15	   fails it. CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 needs *both* controls with OR (`Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.ps1:49-54`, matching ScubaGear's
16	   rego, which also requires exactly two controls). A stricter compliant-only policy passes CIS and fails CISA, so
17	   `entra.ca-require-managed-device` reads Not done in that tenant (see section 3).
18	3. **MT.1014 is admins only.** It needs its own step, `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins`.
19	4. **RequiresOneOf and Not applicable don't mix (engine rule, section 6.2).** `entra.hybrid-join` is `OnlyWhen
20	   hybrid-identity`. In a cloud-only tenant it is Not applicable, which "counts as met", so the group
21	   `[intune.devices-compliant, entra.hybrid-join]` is always met. The managed-device step would show Ready even
22	   with no compliant devices. Proposal: inside a RequiresOneOf group, drop the members that are Not applicable,
23	   and treat a group with no members left as Not applicable.
24	5. **MT.1034 is a narrower probe than MT.1005.** It checks a single What If sign-in (Exchange ActiveSync to
25	   Exchange Online). Recommend taking MT.1034 off the step (details below).
26	6. **Token protection**: every test (CIS.M365.5.2.2.16, ZTA.21941, ZTA.21786) checks a *Windows* policy. Apple has
27	   its own policy and prerequisites. Device registration should be RecommendedFirst, not Requires.
28	7. **Security defaults conflict** is backed by Learn (two pages). No test can verify "off" in a licensed tenant.
29	
30	## 1. Foundation
31	
32	### `entra.emergency-access-excluded`: keep as is, refresh the Note
33	- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access
34	  (`role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md:77,104,108-109,125,254-260`). Learn says to exclude the
35	  accounts (ideally through one group) from enforced policies that block or restrict sign-in, says report-only
36	  policies need no exclusion (77, 104, 125), and says to test their sign-in at least every 90 days (109, 127, 260).
37	  Every CA template repeats the exclusion (`conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:57-60,84`).
38	- Proposed Note: "Exclude these accounts, best through one group, from every enforced policy that can block or
39	  limit sign-in. Report-only policies need no exclusion. Test that they can sign in each quarter."
40	- **MT.1005** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1005.ps1`): every CA policy, *in any state*, excludes the configured
41	  emergency users/groups, or else the user or group that the most policies exclude. Auth-context policies and
42	  service-principal or agent policies are skipped (43-50). Matches the step. It is **stricter than Learn** on
43	  report-only and disabled policies (comment at line 43), so a tenant that follows Learn exactly can fail it.
44	  Suggest limiting it to enabled policies, or noting this in its guide.
45	- **MT.1034** (`Test.MT.1034.ps1:14,63`): for up to five auto-detected emergency users (`Get-MtUser -UserType
46	  EmergencyAccess`, which ignores the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting), the What If API finds no enabled or
47	  report-only policy (`what-if-tool.md:65`) that applies to an Exchange ActiveSync sign-in to Exchange Online.
48	  It **does not prove the same thing**:
49	  it misses policies that target other apps, browsers or desktop clients. It passes when an account is left out by a
50	  role or nested group rather than an exclusion, and it can test different accounts from MT.1005. It is the
51	  "can they sign in" drill (Learn 109, 260), and a narrow version of it. Recommend: **MT.1034 names no step**. Option B is a
52	  state step `entra.emergency-access-can-sign-in` that requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`, but no goal
53	  would contain it (it is a check after the fact, not a prerequisite), so I don't recommend it.
54	- Other tests: ZTA.21835 "Emergency account exists". This is a different state (the account exists), not the exclusion.
55	
56	### `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts` (OnlyWhen `hybrid-identity`): keep
57	- Source as in M1, plus the same instruction in two more templates:
58	  `conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:61,85`, `policy-alt-all-users-compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.md:83`,
59	  `policy-all-users-mfa-strength.md:94`. Learn names it only for policies that target **all users**. The admin-role

62	  every user member of them (148-151). Guest-only policies, legacy-auth blocks and policies that name the sync

64	  principals (73-88), which is harmless under OnlyWhen. It matches the step.

66	  different hardening states, not this step.

166	    with no narrowing condition and no excluded roles except the sync roles. The grant must include `compliantDevice`,
167	    may include `domainJoinedDevice`, nothing else, and uses OR. **Matches.**
168	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.3.7** (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.ps1:41-55`): an enabled policy for All users and all
169	    apps whose grant includes both controls, with operator OR. It does not reject extra OR grants such as MFA,
170	    which upstream does (ScubaGear `AADConfig.rego` requires exactly two controls), so it is looser there and
171	    stricter than CIS on compliant-only. **Same step**, but expect the compliant-only disagreement in headline 2.
172	    Fix it in the test, not the catalogue: add upstream's two-control count. Leave `-SkipHybridJoinCheck` off by default.
173	  - **MT.1014**: narrower (admins), so it moves to the new admin step.
174	  - **ZTA.21892** "All sign-in activity comes from managed devices": despite the title, it checks a *policy* (enabled,
175	    all users, all apps, either control, any operator). This is the matching ZTA ID, though looser.
176	
177	## 4. Goal `token-protection`
178	
179	Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-token-protection
180	(`conditional-access/concept-token-protection.md`), and `deployment-guide-token-protection-windows.md`,
181	`-apple.md`, `-web-apps.md` (URLs `.../deployment-guide-token-protection-windows|apple|web-apps`).
182	- Licence: Entra ID P1 (windows 54, apple 58). It is already on the tests' `License`. No OnlyWhen needed.
183	- Supported: Windows 10+ joined, hybrid joined or registered, and Server 2019+ hybrid joined (concept 91-94).
184	  Apple: macOS 14+ and iOS 16+, MDM-managed only, with the Enterprise SSO plug-in (or Platform SSO on macOS)
185	  (concept 98-101; apple 94). The concept page's table says Apple is GA (67-68) but the device list says "Apple
186	  (Preview)" (98). The page contradicts itself. Resources: Exchange, SharePoint and Teams, plus AVD/W365 on
187	  Windows (76-85). Browser support is preview, ARM only (web-apps guide).
188	
189	### `entra.windows-devices-registered` (state, Unchecked)
190	- Title "Windows devices that sign in are registered with Microsoft Entra ID". Summary "Windows PCs used for Microsoft 365
191	  hold a device identity, so their sign-in tokens can be bound to the device."
192	- Source: concept 54-56, 91-94; windows 124, 205-213 (status 1002 means an unbound request with no device state), 306-314.
193	- Unchecked: "Needs sign-in logs: Graph lists registered devices but not the Windows PCs that sign in without one."
194	- Related tests: none. Hybrid join or Entra join gives the same state. `intune.automatic-enrollment` and
195	  `entra.hybrid-join` are routes to it, but Learn doesn't order them for token protection, so add no edges.
196	
197	### `entra.ca-token-protection`: rename to `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`
198	- Title "Require token protection for sign-in sessions on Windows". Summary "Exchange, SharePoint and Teams accept only device-bound
199	  sign-in tokens from Windows desktop apps, so a stolen token can't be replayed elsewhere."
200	- Why rename: all three tests require a Windows policy, and Learn deploys Apple as a separate policy with different
201	  prerequisites (apple 104-115, 156). An Apple-only tenant would fail a step that doesn't name a platform. IDs aren't
202	  shipped yet, so renaming costs nothing now.
203	- **RecommendedFirst `entra.windows-devices-registered`, not Requires.** With current Windows builds, a user on an
204	  unregistered device is prompted to register (windows 308). Older builds show an error instead (312-314), and
205	  Learn's answer is the report-only pilot, which surfaces 1002. A Requires on an Unchecked state would also keep
206	  the step Unconfirmed in every tenant. Note: "Bound tokens need a registered or joined Windows device. Unregistered
207	  users get a prompt on current builds; report-only logs show who would be affected."
208	- **Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`** (windows 148): the procedure excludes them, as in every CA template.
209	- Optional **RecommendedFirst `entra.ca-block-unknown-platforms`** (new step, verified by **MT.1015**, `Test.MT.1015.ps1:47-49`:
210	  an enabled policy that blocks with `includePlatforms` All. It does not check excluded platforms). Windows 185-190 and
211	  apple 170-177 tell you to also block unknown platforms and require compliance for known ones, so that an attacker can't
212	  dodge the policy by spoofing another platform. That's "more useful", not order. Source:
213	  https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-unknown-unsupported. I would
214	  *not* add `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` as RecommendedFirst, because that would pull the whole compliant-devices goal in.
215	- Rollout (concept 107-115, windows 126-134, 178-181): "Create the policy in report-only for a pilot group, desktop clients
216	  only, for Exchange, SharePoint and Teams.", "Review interactive and non-interactive sign-ins for unbound requests (status
217	  1002 or 1003) over a full working cycle.", "Exclude unsupported device types with a device filter, then turn the policy
218	  On for users who are ready and widen it." (windows 112-120).
219	- Verifying tests:
220	  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.16** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.16.ps1:40-58`): an enabled policy with token protection on, any
221	    included users (a pilot passes), Exchange, SharePoint **and Teams** named explicitly, platforms including Windows,
222	    and client apps exactly `mobileAppsAndDesktopClients`. **Matches** the Windows step. It is the strictest of the three.
223	  - **ZTA.21941** "Token protection policies are configured": an enabled policy with Windows in platforms, token
224	    protection on, some users, and apps All or Exchange plus SharePoint (no Teams). It matches but is looser.
225	  - **ZTA.21786** "User sign-in activity uses token protection": despite the title, it checks a **policy**: enabled,
226	    platforms exactly Windows, desktop clients only, Exchange plus SharePoint, token protection on. It matches. The
227	    title doesn't match the logic: it never reads sign-ins.
228	  - No other test reads `secureSignInSession` (grep across `tests/` and `powershell/`).
229	
230	### Apple: its own pair of steps, but later
231	Learn's Apple guide is a separate track. Configure hardware-backed registration with the SSO plug-in (iOS) or the
232	plug-in or Platform SSO (macOS), and do it *before* users register (apple 115). Devices registered earlier are
233	upgraded when the user signs in again (119, 362-364). Then create a separate report-only policy for iOS and macOS
234	(133-168) and enforce it (349-356). Apple Mail and Calendar are blocked (54, 95). No Maester test checks the SSO
235	plug-in or an Apple token-protection policy. ZTA.24568 ("macOS - Platform SSO is configured and assigned") covers
236	only macOS option B. Recommend *not* adding Apple steps to the first catalogue. When there is a check, add
237	`intune.apple-sso-extension` (Requires on) → `entra.ca-token-protection-apple`, either under a second goal or by
238	turning the goal into "Windows and Apple".
239	
240	## 5. Security defaults as a Conflicts candidate
241	- Learn backs it: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults (`fundamentals/security-defaults.md:251`):
242	  turn security defaults off to replace them with Conditional Access. Also
243	  https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access (`identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access.md:61`):
244	  the two aren't meant to be combined, and creating CA policies stops security defaults from being enabled. Note:
245	  "Security defaults and Conditional Access don't combine. Turn security defaults off before you rely on your own
246	  policies."
247	- No test verifies "off". MT.1021 (`Test.MT.1021.ps1:29-35`) reads `policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy.isEnabled`
248	  but skips any tenant that isn't Free. No other test, ZTA test or EIDSCA test reads that endpoint. Using MT.1021 as the step
249	  "Security defaults are on" would block CA steps only in Free tenants, which can't use CA anyway. The design's
250	  planned readiness check ("Security defaults are off where Conditional Access is licensed", section 11) is still needed.
251	
252	## 6. Draft changes, in short
253	1. Take MT.1034 off `entra.emergency-access-excluded` (it is narrower). Consider limiting MT.1005 to enabled policies.
254	2. Flag MT.1001 (and ZTA.24824) as looser than `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`. Propose tightening MT.1001 to an
255	   enabled all-users, all-apps policy whose grant needs a compliant device (use MT.1014's `requiresDeviceControl` logic).
256	3. Add goal `managed-devices`, with `entra.hybrid-join` (Unchecked, OnlyWhen hybrid) and
257	   `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins` (MT.1014). CIS.M365.5.2.2.9 and CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 stay on
258	   `entra.ca-require-managed-device`, and ZTA.21892 is its ZTA ID.
259	4. Fix the engine rule: Not applicable members of a RequiresOneOf group mustn't satisfy the group.
260	5. Rename `entra.ca-token-protection` → `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`. Make device registration RecommendedFirst.
261	   Add Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`, and optionally `entra.ca-block-unknown-platforms` (MT.1015). Defer Apple.
262	6. Correct section 5's example: CIS 5.2.2.9 requires compliance and only allows hybrid; it is CISA 3.7 that asks
263	   for compliant OR hybrid. Correct section 15's managed-device verifying tests: MT.1014 moves to the admin step.
264	7. Add to `intune.compliance-policies` and `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` the Intune source `device-based-policies.md:77,81-84,99`.
