# Research: Foundation, compliant devices, managed devices, token protection (M2)

Mirror paths are relative to `scratchpad/mirrors/`. All `entra-docs-mirror` paths start `entra-docs-mirror/docs/`.
ZTA logic was read in the installed module `~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/ZeroTrustAssessment/3.1.0/tests/`;
the titles below are the pack catalogue's (2.6.0).

## Headline findings

1. **MT.1001 is looser than `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`.** It passes on any enabled policy with
   `compliantDevice` in the grant, whatever the users, apps or operator (`Test.MT.1001.ps1:41,52`). A "compliant OR
   MFA" policy for one app makes the step Done. ZTA.24824 is just as loose. No test checks the Learn policy (all
   users, all resources, compliant device only). Either tighten MT.1001 or accept that "Done" means only "the control is in use".
2. **The CIS 5.2.2.9 example in section 5 is slightly off.** CIS.M365.5.2.2.9 *requires* `compliantDevice` and only
   *allows* `domainJoinedDevice` beside it (`Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.9.ps1:49`), so a policy that requires only hybrid join
   fails it. CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 needs *both* controls with OR (`Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.ps1:49-54`, matching ScubaGear's
   rego, which also requires exactly two controls). A stricter compliant-only policy passes CIS and fails CISA, so
   `entra.ca-require-managed-device` reads Not done in that tenant (see section 3).
3. **MT.1014 is admins only.** It needs its own step, `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins`.
4. **RequiresOneOf and Not applicable don't mix (engine rule, section 6.2).** `entra.hybrid-join` is `OnlyWhen
   hybrid-identity`. In a cloud-only tenant it is Not applicable, which "counts as met", so the group
   `[intune.devices-compliant, entra.hybrid-join]` is always met. The managed-device step would show Ready even
   with no compliant devices. Proposal: inside a RequiresOneOf group, drop the members that are Not applicable,
   and treat a group with no members left as Not applicable.
5. **MT.1034 is a narrower probe than MT.1005.** It checks a single What If sign-in (Exchange ActiveSync to
   Exchange Online). Recommend taking MT.1034 off the step (details below).
6. **Token protection**: every test (CIS.M365.5.2.2.16, ZTA.21941, ZTA.21786) checks a *Windows* policy. Apple has
   its own policy and prerequisites. Device registration should be RecommendedFirst, not Requires.
7. **Security defaults conflict** is backed by Learn (two pages). No test can verify "off" in a licensed tenant.

## 1. Foundation

### `entra.emergency-access-excluded`: keep as is, refresh the Note
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access
  (`role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md:77,104,108-109,125,254-260`). Learn says to exclude the
  accounts (ideally through one group) from enforced policies that block or restrict sign-in, says report-only
  policies need no exclusion (77, 104, 125), and says to test their sign-in at least every 90 days (109, 127, 260).
  Every CA template repeats the exclusion (`conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:57-60,84`).
- Proposed Note: "Exclude these accounts, best through one group, from every enforced policy that can block or
  limit sign-in. Report-only policies need no exclusion. Test that they can sign in each quarter."
- **MT.1005** (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1005.ps1`): every CA policy, *in any state*, excludes the configured
  emergency users/groups, or else the user or group that the most policies exclude. Auth-context policies and
  service-principal or agent policies are skipped (43-50). Matches the step. It is **stricter than Learn** on
  report-only and disabled policies (comment at line 43), so a tenant that follows Learn exactly can fail it.
  Suggest limiting it to enabled policies, or noting this in its guide.
- **MT.1034** (`Test.MT.1034.ps1:14,63`): for up to five auto-detected emergency users (`Get-MtUser -UserType
  EmergencyAccess`, which ignores the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting), the What If API finds no enabled or
  report-only policy (`what-if-tool.md:65`) that applies to an Exchange ActiveSync sign-in to Exchange Online.
  It **does not prove the same thing**:
  it misses policies that target other apps, browsers or desktop clients. It passes when an account is left out by a
  role or nested group rather than an exclusion, and it can test different accounts from MT.1005. It is the
  "can they sign in" drill (Learn 109, 260), and a narrow version of it. Recommend: **MT.1034 names no step**. Option B is a
  state step `entra.emergency-access-can-sign-in` that requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`, but no goal
  would contain it (it is a check after the fact, not a prerequisite), so I don't recommend it.
- Other tests: ZTA.21835 "Emergency account exists". This is a different state (the account exists), not the exclusion.

### `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts` (OnlyWhen `hybrid-identity`): keep
- Source as in M1, plus the same instruction in two more templates:
  `conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:61,85`, `policy-alt-all-users-compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.md:83`,
  `policy-all-users-mfa-strength.md:94`. Learn names it only for policies that target **all users**. The admin-role
  template (`policy-alt-admin-device-compliand-hybrid.md:93-98`) and the token protection guides don't name it.
- **MT.1020** (`Test.MT.1020.ps1`): enabled policies scoped to all apps (90-99) must exclude the two sync roles or
  every user member of them (148-151). Guest-only policies, legacy-auth blocks and policies that name the sync
  accounts are skipped. It returns **Passed** (not NotApplicable) when there are no sync accounts or only service
  principals (73-88), which is harmless under OnlyWhen. It matches the step.
- Related ZTA: ZTA.24570 (Connect uses service principal credentials) and ZTA.21834 (sync account locked to a named location) are
  different hardening states, not this step.

## 2. Goal `compliant-devices`, re-verified

| Step | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `intune.compliance-policies` | Keep. Add source `intune/device-security/conditional-access-integration/device-based-policies.md:77,81-84` (https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/conditional-access-integration/device-based-policies): set up compliance policies before CA, phase 1 then phase 2. Also `compliance/overview.md:99`: each platform needs a separate policy. Note: "Device-based Conditional Access starts with compliance policies, one per platform, because the policy can only act on the status they report." |
| `intune.automatic-enrollment` | Keep as RecommendedFirst of `intune.devices-compliant`. `enable-automatic-mdm.md:49-52` (devices enroll as they join or register), `:70` (needs Entra ID P1), `:91-99` (MDM user scope None/Some/All). Learn makes it one enrollment route, not a requirement, so RecommendedFirst is right. |
| `intune.devices-compliant` | Keep. Requires `intune.compliance-policies` is backed by `policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:74` (create a policy first, have one compliant device) and `compliance/overview.md:57,142` (policies produce the status; enrolling registers the device). Without a policy, the default setting marks devices Compliant (`overview.md:67-72`), so the Requires rests on meaning, not mechanics. Say so in the Note. |
| `intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant` | Keep as RecommendedFirst. `compliance/overview.md:67-74,144`: switch to Not compliant when CA uses compliance. Also make it RecommendedFirst of the managed-device step (same reason). |
| `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` | Keep the Requires and Rollout. Add a Rollout source: `device-based-policies.md:99` (test with a small group first). |

Verifying tests:
- **ZTA.24541, 24542, 24543, 24545, 24547**: the titles match (Windows, macOS, iOS/iPadOS, Android fully managed,
  Android personal work profile). Each passes when a policy of that type exists **and is assigned**. They are
  **stricter than the step**: a Windows-only tenant fails four of the five, while the step asks for each platform *in use*.
  When ZTA can carry steps, a per-platform split or a new MT check is needed. No ZTA test covers Android
  corporate-owned work profile, AOSP or Linux.
- **ZTA.24546**: the title matches. It passes when the Intune MDM policy's `appliesTo` is not `none`, so Some or All
  (`policies/mobileDeviceManagementPolicies`). Matches.
- **MT.1054** (`tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1054.ps1:40-42`) and **CIS.M365.4.1** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.4.1.ps1:41-44`): both
  read `deviceManagement/settings.secureByDefault -eq $true`. They are identical, so the CIS shim is correct.
- **MT.1001**: see headline 1. **ZTA.24824** ("CA policies block access from noncompliant devices"): any enabled
  policy with `compliantDevice` and no platform filter, or filtered policies that cover Android, iOS, macOS and
  Windows. Any users, apps or operator. Same looseness as MT.1001.

Other tests found (`grep compliantDevice|deviceCompliancePolicies|mobileDeviceManagementPolicies` across `tests/`):
- MT.1214, MT.1216, MT.1228-MT.1237 check **specific settings** in iOS, Android and macOS compliance policies (each fails
  when that platform has no policy, e.g. `Test.MT.1228.ps1:22-28`). They are stricter, different settings, and
  prove no step. The helpers `Get-MtMobileCompliancePolicy` (iOS, Android) and `Get-MtMacOSCompliancePolicy`
  (`powershell/internal/services/intune/`) could back a new MT check for "policy assigned per platform in use". There is no
  Windows helper.
- No MT, CIS, CISA, EIDSCA or ORCA test reads `mobileDeviceManagementPolicies` or checks that a Windows compliance policy exists, so
  `intune.compliance-policies` and `intune.automatic-enrollment` stay **Unchecked**, naming the ZTA IDs.
- CIS.M365.5.2.2.10 and CISA.MS.AAD.3.8 (managed device to register security info), MT.1052 (device code flow)
  and MT.1188 (Private Access apps) use the same controls in other scopes. They prove neither step.

## 3. Managed devices: proposed goal `managed-devices`

**Where it belongs.** `entra.ca-require-managed-device` is an *alternative end state*, not a step towards
compliance-only. Learn lists compliant-or-hybrid policies as what to deploy *instead* when an organisation is not
ready to require compliance for all users (`policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:48-51`). It is also the end
state that CIS 5.2.2.9 and CISA 3.7 ask for. A hybrid tenant can complete it with no Intune at all. Recommend a
separate goal:

```json
{ "Id": "managed-devices", "Title": "Require managed devices",
  "Summary": "Only devices that Intune marks compliant or that are hybrid joined to Microsoft Entra ID can reach Microsoft 365.",
  "Step": "entra.ca-require-managed-device" }
```

### `entra.hybrid-join` (new in the catalogue; draft only)
- Title "Domain-joined Windows devices are hybrid joined to Microsoft Entra ID" (a state). Summary: "Windows PCs joined to
  on-premises AD also have a Microsoft Entra device identity, which Conditional Access can recognise." OnlyWhen `hybrid-identity`.
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/devices/how-to-hybrid-join (`identity/devices/how-to-hybrid-join.md:46-54`).
  Prerequisites: Entra Connect 1.1.819.0 or later syncing the default device attributes and the computer OUs, Hybrid
  Identity Administrator and enterprise admin credentials, AD FS for federated domains, and the device setting
  that lets users register devices (54). No test checks that setting (MT.1070 and CIS 5.1.4.1 restrict *join*,
  which is a different setting). Note: "Needs Entra Connect syncing the computer objects and their device
  attributes, and users allowed to register devices, before PCs can hybrid join."
- Rollout (`identity/devices/hybrid-join-plan.md:130-136`, https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/devices/hybrid-join-plan;
  https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/devices/hybrid-join-control): "Roll out hybrid join to a pilot group of varied
  users first.", "Then enable it for the whole organisation."
- Unchecked: "No check yet. Graph shows hybrid joined devices (trustType ServerAd) but not the domain PCs that are
  missing." (`how-to-hybrid-join-verify.md:83-86`). Possible later: compare with the AD suite's computer objects.

### `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins` (new, for MT.1014)
- Title "Require a compliant or hybrid joined device for administrators". Summary "Admin roles can sign in only from
  a device that Intune marks compliant or that is hybrid joined."
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-alt-admin-device-compliand-hybrid
  (`policy-alt-admin-device-compliand-hybrid.md:50,98,101-102,104-107`).
- Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded` (98). RequiresOneOf `[intune.compliance-policies, entra.hybrid-join]`:
  the hybrid control depends on devices already being hybrid joined (50). Use compliance *policies*, not
  `intune.devices-compliant`, because the readiness share covers all devices, not admin devices. Note: "The
  hybrid joined option works only for devices that are already hybrid joined. Exclude emergency access accounts
  and start in report-only."
- Rollout: report-only, then On (104-107).
- Make it **RecommendedFirst of `entra.ca-require-managed-device`**, backed by `policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:48-50`.
  That page offers the admin policy to organisations that are not ready for all users. Mark it as Maester's
  reading if the reviewers prefer a stricter standard; the fallback is the `privileged-access` goal.
- **MT.1014** (`Test.MT.1014.ps1:83-101`): an enabled policy that covers all 14 admin roles (by role or All users,
  none excluded), all apps, and whose grant needs `compliantDevice` or `domainJoinedDevice` (alone, OR'ed with each
  other, or AND'ed with anything). Matches this step. It also accepts an all-users policy (a superset).

### `entra.ca-require-managed-device`
- Title "Require a compliant or hybrid joined device in Conditional Access". Summary "Sign-ins from devices that are
  neither compliant in Intune nor hybrid joined are blocked."
- Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`, `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`
  (`policy-alt-all-users-compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.md:82-83`). RequiresOneOf `[intune.devices-compliant, entra.hybrid-join]`
  (`policy-alt-all-users-compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.md:55`, `policy-all-users-device-compliance.md:74`,
  `concept-conditional-access-grant.md:111-115,138-140`: compliant needs registered and enrolled devices; the
  hybrid control supports domain-joined Windows only). RecommendedFirst `intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant`,
  `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins`.
- Note (grant page): "Either signal is enough. Compliance needs devices registered and enrolled in Intune; the hybrid
  option covers only domain-joined Windows PCs that are already hybrid joined."
- Rollout (`policy-alt-all-users-compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.md:90-93`): "Create the policy in report-only and review the
  sign-ins it would block.", "Turn it on, keeping the emergency access and sync accounts excluded."
  (No Learn page has the exact all-users policy without MFA. The closest template adds MFA as a third option.)
- Verifying tests:
  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.9** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.9.ps1:41-52`): an enabled policy for All users and all apps
    with no narrowing condition and no excluded roles except the sync roles. The grant must include `compliantDevice`,
    may include `domainJoinedDevice`, nothing else, and uses OR. **Matches.**
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.3.7** (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.ps1:41-55`): an enabled policy for All users and all
    apps whose grant includes both controls, with operator OR. It does not reject extra OR grants such as MFA,
    which upstream does (ScubaGear `AADConfig.rego` requires exactly two controls), so it is looser there and
    stricter than CIS on compliant-only. **Same step**, but expect the compliant-only disagreement in headline 2.
    Fix it in the test, not the catalogue: add upstream's two-control count. Leave `-SkipHybridJoinCheck` off by default.
  - **MT.1014**: narrower (admins), so it moves to the new admin step.
  - **ZTA.21892** "All sign-in activity comes from managed devices": despite the title, it checks a *policy* (enabled,
    all users, all apps, either control, any operator). This is the matching ZTA ID, though looser.

## 4. Goal `token-protection`

Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-token-protection
(`conditional-access/concept-token-protection.md`), and `deployment-guide-token-protection-windows.md`,
`-apple.md`, `-web-apps.md` (URLs `.../deployment-guide-token-protection-windows|apple|web-apps`).
- Licence: Entra ID P1 (windows 54, apple 58). It is already on the tests' `License`. No OnlyWhen needed.
- Supported: Windows 10+ joined, hybrid joined or registered, and Server 2019+ hybrid joined (concept 91-94).
  Apple: macOS 14+ and iOS 16+, MDM-managed only, with the Enterprise SSO plug-in (or Platform SSO on macOS)
  (concept 98-101; apple 94). The concept page's table says Apple is GA (67-68) but the device list says "Apple
  (Preview)" (98). The page contradicts itself. Resources: Exchange, SharePoint and Teams, plus AVD/W365 on
  Windows (76-85). Browser support is preview, ARM only (web-apps guide).

### `entra.windows-devices-registered` (state, Unchecked)
- Title "Windows devices that sign in are registered with Microsoft Entra ID". Summary "Windows PCs used for Microsoft 365
  hold a device identity, so their sign-in tokens can be bound to the device."
- Source: concept 54-56, 91-94; windows 124, 205-213 (status 1002 means an unbound request with no device state), 306-314.
- Unchecked: "Needs sign-in logs: Graph lists registered devices but not the Windows PCs that sign in without one."
- Related tests: none. Hybrid join or Entra join gives the same state. `intune.automatic-enrollment` and
  `entra.hybrid-join` are routes to it, but Learn doesn't order them for token protection, so add no edges.

### `entra.ca-token-protection`: rename to `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`
- Title "Require token protection for sign-in sessions on Windows". Summary "Exchange, SharePoint and Teams accept only device-bound
  sign-in tokens from Windows desktop apps, so a stolen token can't be replayed elsewhere."
- Why rename: all three tests require a Windows policy, and Learn deploys Apple as a separate policy with different
  prerequisites (apple 104-115, 156). An Apple-only tenant would fail a step that doesn't name a platform. IDs aren't
  shipped yet, so renaming costs nothing now.
- **RecommendedFirst `entra.windows-devices-registered`, not Requires.** With current Windows builds, a user on an
  unregistered device is prompted to register (windows 308). Older builds show an error instead (312-314), and
  Learn's answer is the report-only pilot, which surfaces 1002. A Requires on an Unchecked state would also keep
  the step Unconfirmed in every tenant. Note: "Bound tokens need a registered or joined Windows device. Unregistered
  users get a prompt on current builds; report-only logs show who would be affected."
- **Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`** (windows 148): the procedure excludes them, as in every CA template.
- Optional **RecommendedFirst `entra.ca-block-unknown-platforms`** (new step, verified by **MT.1015**, `Test.MT.1015.ps1:47-49`:
  an enabled policy that blocks with `includePlatforms` All. It does not check excluded platforms). Windows 185-190 and
  apple 170-177 tell you to also block unknown platforms and require compliance for known ones, so that an attacker can't
  dodge the policy by spoofing another platform. That's "more useful", not order. Source:
  https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-unknown-unsupported. I would
  *not* add `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` as RecommendedFirst, because that would pull the whole compliant-devices goal in.
- Rollout (concept 107-115, windows 126-134, 178-181): "Create the policy in report-only for a pilot group, desktop clients
  only, for Exchange, SharePoint and Teams.", "Review interactive and non-interactive sign-ins for unbound requests (status
  1002 or 1003) over a full working cycle.", "Exclude unsupported device types with a device filter, then turn the policy
  On for users who are ready and widen it." (windows 112-120).
- Verifying tests:
  - **CIS.M365.5.2.2.16** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.16.ps1:40-58`): an enabled policy with token protection on, any
    included users (a pilot passes), Exchange, SharePoint **and Teams** named explicitly, platforms including Windows,
    and client apps exactly `mobileAppsAndDesktopClients`. **Matches** the Windows step. It is the strictest of the three.
  - **ZTA.21941** "Token protection policies are configured": an enabled policy with Windows in platforms, token
    protection on, some users, and apps All or Exchange plus SharePoint (no Teams). It matches but is looser.
  - **ZTA.21786** "User sign-in activity uses token protection": despite the title, it checks a **policy**: enabled,
    platforms exactly Windows, desktop clients only, Exchange plus SharePoint, token protection on. It matches. The
    title doesn't match the logic: it never reads sign-ins.
  - No other test reads `secureSignInSession` (grep across `tests/` and `powershell/`).

### Apple: its own pair of steps, but later
Learn's Apple guide is a separate track. Configure hardware-backed registration with the SSO plug-in (iOS) or the
plug-in or Platform SSO (macOS), and do it *before* users register (apple 115). Devices registered earlier are
upgraded when the user signs in again (119, 362-364). Then create a separate report-only policy for iOS and macOS
(133-168) and enforce it (349-356). Apple Mail and Calendar are blocked (54, 95). No Maester test checks the SSO
plug-in or an Apple token-protection policy. ZTA.24568 ("macOS - Platform SSO is configured and assigned") covers
only macOS option B. Recommend *not* adding Apple steps to the first catalogue. When there is a check, add
`intune.apple-sso-extension` (Requires on) → `entra.ca-token-protection-apple`, either under a second goal or by
turning the goal into "Windows and Apple".

## 5. Security defaults as a Conflicts candidate
- Learn backs it: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults (`fundamentals/security-defaults.md:251`):
  turn security defaults off to replace them with Conditional Access. Also
  https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access (`identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access.md:61`):
  the two aren't meant to be combined, and creating CA policies stops security defaults from being enabled. Note:
  "Security defaults and Conditional Access don't combine. Turn security defaults off before you rely on your own
  policies."
- No test verifies "off". MT.1021 (`Test.MT.1021.ps1:29-35`) reads `policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy.isEnabled`
  but skips any tenant that isn't Free. No other test, ZTA test or EIDSCA test reads that endpoint. Using MT.1021 as the step
  "Security defaults are on" would block CA steps only in Free tenants, which can't use CA anyway. The design's
  planned readiness check ("Security defaults are off where Conditional Access is licensed", section 11) is still needed.

## 6. Draft changes, in short
1. Take MT.1034 off `entra.emergency-access-excluded` (it is narrower). Consider limiting MT.1005 to enabled policies.
2. Flag MT.1001 (and ZTA.24824) as looser than `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`. Propose tightening MT.1001 to an
   enabled all-users, all-apps policy whose grant needs a compliant device (use MT.1014's `requiresDeviceControl` logic).
3. Add goal `managed-devices`, with `entra.hybrid-join` (Unchecked, OnlyWhen hybrid) and
   `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins` (MT.1014). CIS.M365.5.2.2.9 and CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 stay on
   `entra.ca-require-managed-device`, and ZTA.21892 is its ZTA ID.
4. Fix the engine rule: Not applicable members of a RequiresOneOf group mustn't satisfy the group.
5. Rename `entra.ca-token-protection` → `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`. Make device registration RecommendedFirst.
   Add Requires `entra.emergency-access-excluded`, and optionally `entra.ca-block-unknown-platforms` (MT.1015). Defer Apple.
6. Correct section 5's example: CIS 5.2.2.9 requires compliance and only allows hybrid; it is CISA 3.7 that asks
   for compliant OR hybrid. Correct section 15's managed-device verifying tests: MT.1014 moves to the admin step.
7. Add to `intune.compliance-policies` and `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` the Intune source `device-based-policies.md:77,81-84,99`.
   Note that the ZTA per-platform tests fail platforms the tenant doesn't use.

content.content:
1	# Goal `phishing-resistant-mfa`: findings (M2 expert pass)
2	
3	Mirror root: `scratchpad/mirrors/`. `E` = `entra-docs-mirror/docs/identity/`, `I` = `intune-docs-mirror/intune/`.
4	Page keys used below (URL, mirror file):
5	
6	- DEPLOY: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-deploy-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication (`E/authentication/how-to-deploy-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication.md`)
7	- PREREQ: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-plan-prerequisites-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication (`E/authentication/how-to-plan-prerequisites-...md`)
8	- PASSKEY: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2 (`E/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md`; the brief's `how-to-enable-passkey-fido2.md` does not exist, this is its current page)
9	- TAP: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass (`E/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md`)
10	- STRENGTHS: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths (`E/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths.md`)
11	- HOWITWORKS: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works (`E/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works.md`)
12	- CA-ADMIN: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa (`E/conditional-access/policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa.md`)
13	- CA-ALL: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength (`E/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength.md`). Note: it recommends the *MFA* strength, not phishing-resistant (lines 53-57, 103). Learn has no all-users phishing-resistant template page; DEPLOY lines 252-271 is the all-users source.
14	- INTUNE-PWL: https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/solutions/passwordless (`I/solutions/passwordless.md`)
15	
16	All mirror pages give these as `canonicalUrl` in their front matter (locale removed). ZTA logic was read in the
17	installed ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0 (`~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/ZeroTrustAssessment/3.1.0/tests/`); the
18	catalog is generated from 2.6.0, so three titles have drifted (noted below).
19	
20	## Answers to the brief's questions
21	
22	1. **Learn's order.** Enable methods (DEPLOY 144-147 "must be turned on", 166-173; PASSKEY 49, 66-72) → bootstrap with existing MFA or a TAP (TAP 47-50; DEPLOY 108, 121, 125-127) → users register a portable credential first, then local ones (DEPLOY 95-98, 129, 151-153) → measure, then enforce with an authentication strength (DEPLOY 186, 250, 346-357), admins first "typically" (DEPLOY 202, 352-357). Hard Requires: registration before enforcement (CA-ADMIN 48-50 warns of tenant lockout; HOWITWORKS 109, 113 says users not registered can't reach the resource), emergency access exclusion (CA-ADMIN 87-90, 114; DEPLOY 256). RecommendedFirst: TAP (one of two bootstrap paths), admins before everyone (Learn says "typically ... may change", DEPLOY 202), passkeys before Windows Hello (portable credential first, DEPLOY 129, 153).
23	2. **Windows Hello for Business is one method among several, not a prerequisite.** The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength accepts WHfB *or* platform credential, FIDO2 and multifactor CBA (STRENGTHS 72-76, 86-90). DEPLOY lists WHfB as a recommended *local* credential beside Entra passkey on Windows and CBA (163-164) and never puts it on the enforcement path (350-399). Model it as a member of a `RequiresOneOf` group, not a link in the chain.
24	3. **EIDSCA.** AF01 (state) and AF02 (self-service setup) define "passkeys enabled"; AF03-AF06 are hardening values Learn makes optional. AT01 (state) defines "TAP enabled"; AT02 (one-time) is hardening that Learn does not require. Details per step.
25	4. **Benchmarks.** CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 = all users; ASD.ISM-1872 is a shim of it. CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 and CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 = admin roles only, with different role lists. CISA 3.1 accepts phishing-resistant only; the "or alternative MFA" path is CISA.MS.AAD.3.2, which skips when 3.1 passes (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.2.ps1`) and belongs to an MFA step, not this goal. No MT test checks phishing-resistant strength (MT.1006/MT.1007 accept any MFA).
26	5. **ZTA.** 21839, 24551, 21782, 21783 match their steps. 21781 and 21784 do not (see step 8 and 9). Extra IDs found: 21838, 21840, 21845, 21846, 21801, 24568.
27	6. **Admin registration before admin enforcement** is Learn-backed and is a hard Requires (CA-ADMIN 48-50). **All-user registration** is backed too (DEPLOY 95, 250; HOWITWORKS 113) and needs its own step, Unchecked until the section 11 readiness check exists (ZTA.21801 checks it).
28	
29	## Proposed steps, in order
30	
31	### 1. `entra.passkeys-enabled` (keep)
32	- Title: Enable passkeys (FIDO2) in the Authentication methods policy
33	- Summary: Users in scope can register a passkey on a security key, in Microsoft Authenticator or with a passkey provider.
34	- Relationships: none.
35	- Sources: PASSKEY 49 (users can register only after the steps), 66-72 (ordered steps; profiles, then targets), 154 (self-service setup must be Yes, or users can't register at Security info). DEPLOY 144-146.
36	  Note: "Turn on Passkey (FIDO2) for the users who will register, and allow self-service setup, or users can't add a passkey at Security info."
37	- Rollout (DEPLOY 190-195, PASSKEY 98-103, DEPLOY 138): "Enable it for a pilot group that includes admins and other personas, and watch registrations in the Authentication methods activity report." / "Give admins a passkey profile that allows device-bound passkeys only, with attestation enforced." / "Widen the targets persona by persona."
38	- Verifying tests:
39	  - EIDSCA.AF01 (generated): `Fido2.state -eq 'enabled'`. **Matches.**
40	  - EIDSCA.AF02 (generated): `isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed -eq true`, skipped when FIDO2 is off. **Matches** (Learn line 154 makes it part of users being able to register).
41	  - EIDSCA.AF03 (attestation), AF04 (key restrictions enforced), AF05 (AAGUID list non-empty), AF06 (allow/block list set): **name no step.** Learn makes these optional per profile: PASSKEY 171-172, 178 ("only if your organization wants" specific models), and synced passkeys can't be attested (221), while Learn recommends synced passkeys for non-admins (DEPLOY 136). Requiring AF03 here would contradict that.
42	  - ZTA.21839 "Passkey authentication method enabled": state enabled and includeTargets non-empty (3.1.0 lines 28-37, 80). **Matches.** ZTA.21838 "Security key authentication method enabled": state enabled only. **Matches.** ZTA.21840 (attestation): no step.
43	
44	### 2. `entra.temporary-access-pass` (keep)
45	- Title: Enable Temporary Access Pass
46	- Summary: Admins can issue a time-limited pass so a user with no MFA method can sign in and register a passwordless one.
47	- Relationships: none.
48	- Sources: TAP 58-60 (enable the method and scope users before anyone can sign in with a pass), 47-52 (one of two ways to bootstrap). DEPLOY 108, 114, 121.
49	  Note: "A pass works only for users in scope of the TAP method policy, so enable it and target the users who onboard or recover with it."
50	- Verifying tests:
51	  - EIDSCA.AT01 (generated): `TemporaryAccessPass.state -eq 'enabled'`. **Matches.**
52	  - EIDSCA.AT02 (generated): `isUsableOnce -eq true`. **Name no step.** Learn's default is false (TAP 86) and it documents both single-use and multiuse TAPs as supported for device setup (TAP 170-173). It is hardening, not "enabled".
53	  - ZTA.21845 "Temporary access pass is enabled": **stricter**; passes only when TAP targets all users *and* an enabled CA policy on the Register security information user action requires a strength that includes TAP (3.1.0 lines 33-60, 83). HOWITWORKS 78-85 shows that pattern as an example, not a prerequisite. Leave it off this step. ZTA.21846 (one-time use; 3.1.0 title now "Restrict Temporary Access Pass to Single Use"): no step.
54	
55	### 3. `intune.windows-hello` (rename from `entra.windows-hello`)
56	- Rename reason: WHfB has no Entra Authentication methods policy entry; Intune (or Group Policy) delivers it (INTUNE-PWL 128), and its only check, ZTA.24551, reads Intune (`deviceManagement/deviceEnrollmentConfigurations` and settings catalog `usepassportforwork`).
57	- Title: Configure Windows Hello for Business for Windows devices
58	- Summary: Users provision a Windows Hello for Business key on their Windows devices and sign in with a PIN or biometric.
59	- RecommendedFirst: `entra.passkeys-enabled`. Source DEPLOY 129, 153 (the first credential should be portable, and it bootstraps WHfB on the PC).
60	  Note: "Give users a portable passkey first. They can then use it to set up Windows Hello for Business on each PC."
61	- Sources for the step itself: DEPLOY 163-170 (recommended local credential on Windows; cloud Kerberos trust for synced users); INTUNE-PWL 128.
62	- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24551) once its results can name steps."
63	- ZTA.24551: passes when the tenant-wide WHfB enrollment config is enabled or an assigned settings catalog policy sets UsePassportForWork (3.1.0 line 66). **Matches.** Catalog title "Windows Hello for Business Policy is Configured and Assigned" is right for 2.6.0; 3.1.0 renamed it "Authentication on Windows uses Windows Hello for Business" (line 16) with the same logic. Fails tenants that deploy WHfB by Group Policy.
64	
65	### 4. New, optional: `entra.certificate-based-auth` and `intune.macos-platform-sso`
66	Learn names both as phishing-resistant methods that satisfy the strength (STRENGTHS 74-76, 89-90; DEPLOY 147, 163-164, 172). Add them to the `RequiresOneOf` group so a CBA-only or Mac-only tenant is not shown as blocked. They add no false signal: the group already contains Unchecked members, so it can only be Unconfirmed, never Blocked, until checks exist.
67	- `entra.certificate-based-auth`: "Configure Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication" / "Users sign in with a smart card or certificate that Entra accepts as multifactor." Source DEPLOY 147 (configure the policy OID and affinity bindings so CBA counts as MFA; use it only if needed); HOWITWORKS 119 (admins set it up, users can't self-register). Note: "Bind the certificate policy OIDs as multifactor, or CBA sign-ins won't satisfy the phishing-resistant strength." Unchecked: "No Maester or Zero Trust Assessment check yet."
68	- `intune.macos-platform-sso`: "Configure Platform SSO with the Secure Enclave key for macOS" / "Mac users sign in with a hardware-bound key that counts as phishing-resistant." Source DEPLOY 172 (needs MDM enrollment; deploy the Secure Enclave key method), https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-macos (`I/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-macos.md`). Unchecked: ZTA.24568 (catalog "macOS - Platform SSO is configured and assigned"; 3.1.0 renamed it "Platform SSO is configured to strengthen authentication on macOS devices").
69	- If the owner wants the catalogue lean, drop both; the group then has two members.
70	
71	### 5. `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins` (rename from `entra.phishing-resistant-registered`)
72	- Rename reason: the draft ID reads as all users but its check is privileged users only; step 7 needs the all-users state.
73	- Title: Administrators have a phishing-resistant method registered
74	- Summary: Every account that holds an admin role can already sign in with a passkey, Windows Hello for Business or a certificate.
75	- RequiresOneOf: [`entra.passkeys-enabled`, `intune.windows-hello`, `entra.certificate-based-auth`, `intune.macos-platform-sso`]. Sources: HOWITWORKS 58 (users register only methods they are enabled for); STRENGTHS 80 (the strength's methods must be enabled by admins and registered by users), 72-76.
76	  Note: "Admins can register only a method the tenant has enabled. Any method in the phishing-resistant strength will do."
77	- RecommendedFirst: `entra.temporary-access-pass`. Sources: CA-ADMIN 50 (register via TAP or by registering a passkey), TAP 47-50, DEPLOY 121, 125-127, PASSKEY 136 (registering a passkey needs MFA in the last five minutes).
78	  Note: "An admin with no MFA method needs a Temporary Access Pass to register their first passkey. Admins with MFA can use it instead."
79	  Considered and rejected: `RequiresOneOf [entra.temporary-access-pass, entra.mfa-registered]`. Learn backs it per user, but `entra.mfa-registered` measures 95% of all members, so it would misreport admins.
80	- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.21782) once its results can name steps."
81	- ZTA.21782 "Privileged accounts have phishing-resistant methods registered": every user holding a directory role has a device-bound passkey, Authenticator passkey or WHfB registered (3.1.0 lines 32, 44). **Matches**, slightly stricter: synced passkeys, CBA and platform credential don't count.
82	- Recommend that the section 11 readiness check for registration also covers admins (a scope parameter), so this step gets a Maester check.
83	
84	### 6. `entra.phishing-resistant-admins` (keep)
85	- Title: Require phishing-resistant MFA for administrator roles
86	- Summary: Accounts in admin roles must sign in with a phishing-resistant method to reach any resource.
87	- Requires: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins`. Source CA-ADMIN 48-50.
88	  Note: "Admins who haven't registered a phishing-resistant method are locked out when the policy turns on, which can lock you out of the tenant."
89	- Requires: `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Source CA-ADMIN 87-90, 114.
90	  Note: "Exclude the emergency access accounts so a policy mistake can't lock every administrator out."
91	- No `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`: the policy targets directory roles, and CA-ADMIN 52-67 does not list Directory Synchronization Accounts.
92	- Rollout (CA-ADMIN 119-122; DEPLOY 352-355): "Create the policy for the admin roles in report-only mode and review the sign-ins it would block." / "Turn it on for admins on Windows and iOS first, then macOS and Android." / "Keep the emergency access accounts excluded."
93	- Verifying tests (role lists differ; Learn's list is 14 roles "at least", CA-ADMIN 52-69):
94	  - CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.5.ps1`): an enabled policy whose includeRoles cover CIS's 15 roles (Learn's 14 plus Global Reader, `powershell/internal/checks/cis/entra/Get-MtCisAdministratorRole.ps1` 20-34), all resources with no app exclusions, no narrowing platform/location/client conditions, no risk conditions, and a strength whose allowedCombinations are a non-empty subset of WHfB, FIDO2, multifactor CBA (lines 41-57). Not a shim. **Matches** (closest to Learn; one role stricter).
95	  - CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.6.ps1`): enabled, all apps, strength `displayName -eq 'Phishing-resistant MFA'` (custom strengths fail), includeRoles contain CISA's 8 highly privileged roles (`powershell/public/services/entra/Get-MtRole.ps1` 25-34; lines 38-46). Not a shim. **Different definition of done:** it covers 8 roles, leaves out 7 of Learn's (Authentication, Billing, Conditional Access, Helpdesk, Password, Privileged Authentication, Security Administrator), adds Hybrid Identity Administrator, which neither Learn nor CIS lists, and rejects custom strengths. Neither test's role list contains the other's, so they pass and fail in the same run. Recommendation: CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 alone names this step; CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 names none. Alternative, if CISA coverage on the path matters more than the section 5 rule: name both and say in How to fix that the policy must cover both lists (union) with the built-in strength.
96	  - ZTA.21783: every built-in role marked `isPrivileged` (far more than 14) is in includeRoles of a policy using a strength made only of phishing-resistant methods; it counts report-only policies (3.1.0 lines 32, 36-68). Broader roles, looser state; title matches. Report only.
97	  - ZTA.21781: **drop.** Its title is about sign-in activity, not a policy, and in 3.1.0 it always ends `SkippedBecause UnderConstruction` (lines 23, 37); as a verifier it would make the step Unknown forever.
98	- Finding: CIS 5.2.2.5, CISA 3.6 and ZTA.21783 only read includeRoles, so a tenant whose only control is the all-users policy (step 9) stays Not done here. That matches Learn, which keeps a dedicated admin policy (CA-ADMIN), but How to fix should say so.
99	
100	### 7. New: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all`
101	- Title: Users have a phishing-resistant method registered
102	- Summary: Most users can already sign in with a passkey, Windows Hello for Business or a certificate on the devices they use.
103	- RequiresOneOf: the same group as step 5 (same sources, same Note).
104	- RecommendedFirst: `entra.temporary-access-pass` (same sources as step 5; DEPLOY 127 for new users and users with no MFA).
105	  Note: "New users and users with no MFA method need a Temporary Access Pass to register their first phishing-resistant credential."
106	- Sources for the state itself: DEPLOY 95-98 (register a portable credential, then local ones; enforce after registration), 186, 244-246 (enrollment readiness).
107	- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. A readiness check is planned; the Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.21801) once its results can name steps."
108	- ZTA.21801 "Users have strong authentication methods configured": every enabled user has a device-bound passkey, Authenticator passkey or WHfB registered (3.1.0 lines 44-60), i.e. 100%, versus the planned 95% `MinimumShare`. Title is vaguer than the logic but matches.
109	
110	### 8. `entra.phishing-resistant-all` (keep; the goal's step)
111	- Title: Require phishing-resistant MFA for all users
112	- Summary: Every user must sign in with a phishing-resistant method to reach any resource.
113	- Requires: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all`. Sources HOWITWORKS 109, 113 (users must be registered first; otherwise they can't reach the resource until they register); DEPLOY 250 (enforce once users are ready).
114	  Note: "Users who haven't registered a phishing-resistant method are blocked from every resource once it's enforced. Get them registered first."
115	- Requires: `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Source DEPLOY 254-256 (all users, excluding break-glass accounts).
116	  Note: "Exclude the emergency access accounts from the all-users policy."
117	- Requires: `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`. Source CA-ALL 94 (all-users authentication-strength policy: exclude the Directory Synchronization Accounts role under hybrid identity). DEPLOY does not repeat it, so this relies on the general all-users template.
118	  Note: "With Connect or Cloud Sync, exclude the Directory Synchronization Accounts role. Sync accounts can't do phishing-resistant MFA."
119	- RecommendedFirst: `entra.phishing-resistant-admins`. Source DEPLOY 202, 352-357.
120	  Note: "Learn typically starts with admins and then moves to other users, by device platform. The order can change for your organization."
121	- Rollout (DEPLOY 252-261, 263-271, 335-342, 389-399): "Create the all-users policy in report-only mode early, before registration campaigns, to record which sign-ins it would block." / "Enforce it in waves, one policy per device platform, for groups of users who are ready." / "Once almost every user is in a ready group, turn the all-users policy on and remove the per-platform policies."
122	- Verifying tests:
123	  - CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.1.ps1` 39-55): an enabled policy with includeUsers All, includeApplications All, and the built-in strength (id ...0004) or a custom strength limited to WHfB, FIDO2, multifactor CBA. Does not check exclusions or narrowing conditions. **Matches.** Phishing-resistant only; no "or" path.
124	  - ASD.ISM-1872 (`tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1872.ps1` 41): **shim** of CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 (`return Test-MtCisaPhishResistant`); same step.
125	  - ZTA.21784: **drop.** It accepts any strength that contains at least one phishing-resistant method (3.1.0 lines 110-131). The built-in *MFA* strength contains FIDO2, WHfB and CBA (STRENGTHS 86-90), so an all-users MFA policy passes. It also fails when any policy excludes a user (lines 147-152), so it fails a tenant that excludes break-glass accounts by user, against `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Its title (sign-in activity) also doesn't describe its logic.
126	- No CIS or MT test checks phishing-resistant MFA for all users.
127	
128	## Final step list (draft section 15 row)
129	
130	`entra.passkeys-enabled` and `entra.temporary-access-pass` → `intune.windows-hello` (recommended after passkeys)
131	[+ optional `entra.certificate-based-auth`, `intune.macos-platform-sso`] → `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins`
132	(requires one method; TAP recommended first) → `entra.phishing-resistant-admins` (requires admin registration and
133	emergency access exclusion) → `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all` (new, Unchecked) → `entra.phishing-resistant-all`
134	(requires all-user registration, emergency access and sync exclusions; admins recommended first).
135	
136	Verifying tests: EIDSCA.AF01, AF02 (ZTA.21839, 21838) · EIDSCA.AT01 · unchecked (ZTA.24551) · unchecked (ZTA.21782) ·
137	CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 (ZTA.21783) · unchecked (ZTA.21801) · CISA.MS.AAD.3.1, ASD.ISM-1872.
138	
139	## Changes to the draft, with evidence
140	
141	| Draft | Change | Why |
142	| --- | --- | --- |
143	| `entra.windows-hello` as a link in the chain | `intune.windows-hello`, a `RequiresOneOf` member | STRENGTHS 72-76, 86-90; DEPLOY 163-170; INTUNE-PWL 128; check reads Intune |
144	| `entra.phishing-resistant-registered` (admins) | rename `-registered-admins`; add `-registered-all` | Draft ID suggests all users; DEPLOY 95, 250 and HOWITWORKS 113 back all-user registration before enforcement |
145	| EIDSCA.AF03-AF06 | no step | Optional per PASSKEY 171-178; attestation blocks synced passkeys (221), which DEPLOY 136 recommends |
146	| EIDSCA.AT02 | no step | TAP 86, 170-173: multiuse is the default and supported |
147	| CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 | no step (or name it with an explicit union rule) | 8 roles incl. Hybrid Identity Admin vs CIS 15 vs Learn 14; built-in strength only |
148	| ZTA.21781 | drop | Sign-in activity, UnderConstruction in 3.1.0 |
149	| ZTA.21784 | drop | Accepts MFA strength; fails on user exclusions |
150	| TAP as a sequential prerequisite | RecommendedFirst on the two registration states | TAP is one of two bootstrap paths (TAP 47-50; DEPLOY 125-127) |
151	| Admins before all users | RecommendedFirst, not Requires | DEPLOY 202 says "typically" and that it can change |
152	
153	Test-quality notes for follow-up (not step changes): CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 matches the strength by display name, while CISA
154	3.1 in the same suite accepts custom strengths; ZTA.21783 counts report-only policies (its own TODO, 3.1.0 line 32).

# Goal `phishing-resistant-mfa`: findings (M2 expert pass)

Mirror root: `scratchpad/mirrors/`. `E` = `entra-docs-mirror/docs/identity/`, `I` = `intune-docs-mirror/intune/`.
Page keys used below (URL, mirror file):

- DEPLOY: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-deploy-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication (`E/authentication/how-to-deploy-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication.md`)
- PREREQ: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-plan-prerequisites-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication (`E/authentication/how-to-plan-prerequisites-...md`)
- PASSKEY: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2 (`E/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md`; the brief's `how-to-enable-passkey-fido2.md` does not exist, this is its current page)
- TAP: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass (`E/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md`)
- STRENGTHS: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths (`E/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths.md`)
- HOWITWORKS: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works (`E/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works.md`)
- CA-ADMIN: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa (`E/conditional-access/policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa.md`)
- CA-ALL: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength (`E/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength.md`). Note: it recommends the *MFA* strength, not phishing-resistant (lines 53-57, 103). Learn has no all-users phishing-resistant template page; DEPLOY lines 252-271 is the all-users source.
- INTUNE-PWL: https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/solutions/passwordless (`I/solutions/passwordless.md`)

All mirror pages give these as `canonicalUrl` in their front matter (locale removed). ZTA logic was read in the
installed ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0 (`~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/ZeroTrustAssessment/3.1.0/tests/`); the
catalog is generated from 2.6.0, so three titles have drifted (noted below).

## Answers to the brief's questions

1. **Learn's order.** Enable methods (DEPLOY 144-147 "must be turned on", 166-173; PASSKEY 49, 66-72) → bootstrap with existing MFA or a TAP (TAP 47-50; DEPLOY 108, 121, 125-127) → users register a portable credential first, then local ones (DEPLOY 95-98, 129, 151-153) → measure, then enforce with an authentication strength (DEPLOY 186, 250, 346-357), admins first "typically" (DEPLOY 202, 352-357). Hard Requires: registration before enforcement (CA-ADMIN 48-50 warns of tenant lockout; HOWITWORKS 109, 113 says users not registered can't reach the resource), emergency access exclusion (CA-ADMIN 87-90, 114; DEPLOY 256). RecommendedFirst: TAP (one of two bootstrap paths), admins before everyone (Learn says "typically ... may change", DEPLOY 202), passkeys before Windows Hello (portable credential first, DEPLOY 129, 153).
2. **Windows Hello for Business is one method among several, not a prerequisite.** The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength accepts WHfB *or* platform credential, FIDO2 and multifactor CBA (STRENGTHS 72-76, 86-90). DEPLOY lists WHfB as a recommended *local* credential beside Entra passkey on Windows and CBA (163-164) and never puts it on the enforcement path (350-399). Model it as a member of a `RequiresOneOf` group, not a link in the chain.
3. **EIDSCA.** AF01 (state) and AF02 (self-service setup) define "passkeys enabled"; AF03-AF06 are hardening values Learn makes optional. AT01 (state) defines "TAP enabled"; AT02 (one-time) is hardening that Learn does not require. Details per step.
4. **Benchmarks.** CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 = all users; ASD.ISM-1872 is a shim of it. CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 and CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 = admin roles only, with different role lists. CISA 3.1 accepts phishing-resistant only; the "or alternative MFA" path is CISA.MS.AAD.3.2, which skips when 3.1 passes (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.2.ps1`) and belongs to an MFA step, not this goal. No MT test checks phishing-resistant strength (MT.1006/MT.1007 accept any MFA).
5. **ZTA.** 21839, 24551, 21782, 21783 match their steps. 21781 and 21784 do not (see step 8 and 9). Extra IDs found: 21838, 21840, 21845, 21846, 21801, 24568.
6. **Admin registration before admin enforcement** is Learn-backed and is a hard Requires (CA-ADMIN 48-50). **All-user registration** is backed too (DEPLOY 95, 250; HOWITWORKS 113) and needs its own step, Unchecked until the section 11 readiness check exists (ZTA.21801 checks it).

## Proposed steps, in order

### 1. `entra.passkeys-enabled` (keep)
- Title: Enable passkeys (FIDO2) in the Authentication methods policy
- Summary: Users in scope can register a passkey on a security key, in Microsoft Authenticator or with a passkey provider.
- Relationships: none.
- Sources: PASSKEY 49 (users can register only after the steps), 66-72 (ordered steps; profiles, then targets), 154 (self-service setup must be Yes, or users can't register at Security info). DEPLOY 144-146.
  Note: "Turn on Passkey (FIDO2) for the users who will register, and allow self-service setup, or users can't add a passkey at Security info."
- Rollout (DEPLOY 190-195, PASSKEY 98-103, DEPLOY 138): "Enable it for a pilot group that includes admins and other personas, and watch registrations in the Authentication methods activity report." / "Give admins a passkey profile that allows device-bound passkeys only, with attestation enforced." / "Widen the targets persona by persona."
- Verifying tests:
  - EIDSCA.AF01 (generated): `Fido2.state -eq 'enabled'`. **Matches.**
  - EIDSCA.AF02 (generated): `isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed -eq true`, skipped when FIDO2 is off. **Matches** (Learn line 154 makes it part of users being able to register).
  - EIDSCA.AF03 (attestation), AF04 (key restrictions enforced), AF05 (AAGUID list non-empty), AF06 (allow/block list set): **name no step.** Learn makes these optional per profile: PASSKEY 171-172, 178 ("only if your organization wants" specific models), and synced passkeys can't be attested (221), while Learn recommends synced passkeys for non-admins (DEPLOY 136). Requiring AF03 here would contradict that.
  - ZTA.21839 "Passkey authentication method enabled": state enabled and includeTargets non-empty (3.1.0 lines 28-37, 80). **Matches.** ZTA.21838 "Security key authentication method enabled": state enabled only. **Matches.** ZTA.21840 (attestation): no step.

### 2. `entra.temporary-access-pass` (keep)
- Title: Enable Temporary Access Pass
- Summary: Admins can issue a time-limited pass so a user with no MFA method can sign in and register a passwordless one.
- Relationships: none.
- Sources: TAP 58-60 (enable the method and scope users before anyone can sign in with a pass), 47-52 (one of two ways to bootstrap). DEPLOY 108, 114, 121.
  Note: "A pass works only for users in scope of the TAP method policy, so enable it and target the users who onboard or recover with it."
- Verifying tests:
  - EIDSCA.AT01 (generated): `TemporaryAccessPass.state -eq 'enabled'`. **Matches.**
  - EIDSCA.AT02 (generated): `isUsableOnce -eq true`. **Name no step.** Learn's default is false (TAP 86) and it documents both single-use and multiuse TAPs as supported for device setup (TAP 170-173). It is hardening, not "enabled".
  - ZTA.21845 "Temporary access pass is enabled": **stricter**; passes only when TAP targets all users *and* an enabled CA policy on the Register security information user action requires a strength that includes TAP (3.1.0 lines 33-60, 83). HOWITWORKS 78-85 shows that pattern as an example, not a prerequisite. Leave it off this step. ZTA.21846 (one-time use; 3.1.0 title now "Restrict Temporary Access Pass to Single Use"): no step.

### 3. `intune.windows-hello` (rename from `entra.windows-hello`)
- Rename reason: WHfB has no Entra Authentication methods policy entry; Intune (or Group Policy) delivers it (INTUNE-PWL 128), and its only check, ZTA.24551, reads Intune (`deviceManagement/deviceEnrollmentConfigurations` and settings catalog `usepassportforwork`).
- Title: Configure Windows Hello for Business for Windows devices
- Summary: Users provision a Windows Hello for Business key on their Windows devices and sign in with a PIN or biometric.
- RecommendedFirst: `entra.passkeys-enabled`. Source DEPLOY 129, 153 (the first credential should be portable, and it bootstraps WHfB on the PC).
  Note: "Give users a portable passkey first. They can then use it to set up Windows Hello for Business on each PC."
- Sources for the step itself: DEPLOY 163-170 (recommended local credential on Windows; cloud Kerberos trust for synced users); INTUNE-PWL 128.
- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24551) once its results can name steps."
- ZTA.24551: passes when the tenant-wide WHfB enrollment config is enabled or an assigned settings catalog policy sets UsePassportForWork (3.1.0 line 66). **Matches.** Catalog title "Windows Hello for Business Policy is Configured and Assigned" is right for 2.6.0; 3.1.0 renamed it "Authentication on Windows uses Windows Hello for Business" (line 16) with the same logic. Fails tenants that deploy WHfB by Group Policy.

### 4. New, optional: `entra.certificate-based-auth` and `intune.macos-platform-sso`
Learn names both as phishing-resistant methods that satisfy the strength (STRENGTHS 74-76, 89-90; DEPLOY 147, 163-164, 172). Add them to the `RequiresOneOf` group so a CBA-only or Mac-only tenant is not shown as blocked. They add no false signal: the group already contains Unchecked members, so it can only be Unconfirmed, never Blocked, until checks exist.
- `entra.certificate-based-auth`: "Configure Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication" / "Users sign in with a smart card or certificate that Entra accepts as multifactor." Source DEPLOY 147 (configure the policy OID and affinity bindings so CBA counts as MFA; use it only if needed); HOWITWORKS 119 (admins set it up, users can't self-register). Note: "Bind the certificate policy OIDs as multifactor, or CBA sign-ins won't satisfy the phishing-resistant strength." Unchecked: "No Maester or Zero Trust Assessment check yet."
- `intune.macos-platform-sso`: "Configure Platform SSO with the Secure Enclave key for macOS" / "Mac users sign in with a hardware-bound key that counts as phishing-resistant." Source DEPLOY 172 (needs MDM enrollment; deploy the Secure Enclave key method), https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-macos (`I/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-macos.md`). Unchecked: ZTA.24568 (catalog "macOS - Platform SSO is configured and assigned"; 3.1.0 renamed it "Platform SSO is configured to strengthen authentication on macOS devices").
- If the owner wants the catalogue lean, drop both; the group then has two members.

### 5. `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins` (rename from `entra.phishing-resistant-registered`)
- Rename reason: the draft ID reads as all users but its check is privileged users only; step 7 needs the all-users state.
- Title: Administrators have a phishing-resistant method registered
- Summary: Every account that holds an admin role can already sign in with a passkey, Windows Hello for Business or a certificate.
- RequiresOneOf: [`entra.passkeys-enabled`, `intune.windows-hello`, `entra.certificate-based-auth`, `intune.macos-platform-sso`]. Sources: HOWITWORKS 58 (users register only methods they are enabled for); STRENGTHS 80 (the strength's methods must be enabled by admins and registered by users), 72-76.
  Note: "Admins can register only a method the tenant has enabled. Any method in the phishing-resistant strength will do."
- RecommendedFirst: `entra.temporary-access-pass`. Sources: CA-ADMIN 50 (register via TAP or by registering a passkey), TAP 47-50, DEPLOY 121, 125-127, PASSKEY 136 (registering a passkey needs MFA in the last five minutes).
  Note: "An admin with no MFA method needs a Temporary Access Pass to register their first passkey. Admins with MFA can use it instead."
  Considered and rejected: `RequiresOneOf [entra.temporary-access-pass, entra.mfa-registered]`. Learn backs it per user, but `entra.mfa-registered` measures 95% of all members, so it would misreport admins.
- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.21782) once its results can name steps."
- ZTA.21782 "Privileged accounts have phishing-resistant methods registered": every user holding a directory role has a device-bound passkey, Authenticator passkey or WHfB registered (3.1.0 lines 32, 44). **Matches**, slightly stricter: synced passkeys, CBA and platform credential don't count.
- Recommend that the section 11 readiness check for registration also covers admins (a scope parameter), so this step gets a Maester check.

### 6. `entra.phishing-resistant-admins` (keep)
- Title: Require phishing-resistant MFA for administrator roles
- Summary: Accounts in admin roles must sign in with a phishing-resistant method to reach any resource.
- Requires: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins`. Source CA-ADMIN 48-50.
  Note: "Admins who haven't registered a phishing-resistant method are locked out when the policy turns on, which can lock you out of the tenant."
- Requires: `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Source CA-ADMIN 87-90, 114.
  Note: "Exclude the emergency access accounts so a policy mistake can't lock every administrator out."
- No `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`: the policy targets directory roles, and CA-ADMIN 52-67 does not list Directory Synchronization Accounts.
- Rollout (CA-ADMIN 119-122; DEPLOY 352-355): "Create the policy for the admin roles in report-only mode and review the sign-ins it would block." / "Turn it on for admins on Windows and iOS first, then macOS and Android." / "Keep the emergency access accounts excluded."
- Verifying tests (role lists differ; Learn's list is 14 roles "at least", CA-ADMIN 52-69):
  - CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.5.ps1`): an enabled policy whose includeRoles cover CIS's 15 roles (Learn's 14 plus Global Reader, `powershell/internal/checks/cis/entra/Get-MtCisAdministratorRole.ps1` 20-34), all resources with no app exclusions, no narrowing platform/location/client conditions, no risk conditions, and a strength whose allowedCombinations are a non-empty subset of WHfB, FIDO2, multifactor CBA (lines 41-57). Not a shim. **Matches** (closest to Learn; one role stricter).
  - CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.6.ps1`): enabled, all apps, strength `displayName -eq 'Phishing-resistant MFA'` (custom strengths fail), includeRoles contain CISA's 8 highly privileged roles (`powershell/public/services/entra/Get-MtRole.ps1` 25-34; lines 38-46). Not a shim. **Different definition of done:** it covers 8 roles, leaves out 7 of Learn's (Authentication, Billing, Conditional Access, Helpdesk, Password, Privileged Authentication, Security Administrator), adds Hybrid Identity Administrator, which neither Learn nor CIS lists, and rejects custom strengths. Neither test's role list contains the other's, so they pass and fail in the same run. Recommendation: CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 alone names this step; CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 names none. Alternative, if CISA coverage on the path matters more than the section 5 rule: name both and say in How to fix that the policy must cover both lists (union) with the built-in strength.
  - ZTA.21783: every built-in role marked `isPrivileged` (far more than 14) is in includeRoles of a policy using a strength made only of phishing-resistant methods; it counts report-only policies (3.1.0 lines 32, 36-68). Broader roles, looser state; title matches. Report only.
  - ZTA.21781: **drop.** Its title is about sign-in activity, not a policy, and in 3.1.0 it always ends `SkippedBecause UnderConstruction` (lines 23, 37); as a verifier it would make the step Unknown forever.
- Finding: CIS 5.2.2.5, CISA 3.6 and ZTA.21783 only read includeRoles, so a tenant whose only control is the all-users policy (step 9) stays Not done here. That matches Learn, which keeps a dedicated admin policy (CA-ADMIN), but How to fix should say so.

### 7. New: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all`
- Title: Users have a phishing-resistant method registered
- Summary: Most users can already sign in with a passkey, Windows Hello for Business or a certificate on the devices they use.
- RequiresOneOf: the same group as step 5 (same sources, same Note).
- RecommendedFirst: `entra.temporary-access-pass` (same sources as step 5; DEPLOY 127 for new users and users with no MFA).
  Note: "New users and users with no MFA method need a Temporary Access Pass to register their first phishing-resistant credential."
- Sources for the state itself: DEPLOY 95-98 (register a portable credential, then local ones; enforce after registration), 186, 244-246 (enrollment readiness).
- Unchecked: "No Maester check yet. A readiness check is planned; the Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.21801) once its results can name steps."
- ZTA.21801 "Users have strong authentication methods configured": every enabled user has a device-bound passkey, Authenticator passkey or WHfB registered (3.1.0 lines 44-60), i.e. 100%, versus the planned 95% `MinimumShare`. Title is vaguer than the logic but matches.

### 8. `entra.phishing-resistant-all` (keep; the goal's step)
- Title: Require phishing-resistant MFA for all users
- Summary: Every user must sign in with a phishing-resistant method to reach any resource.
- Requires: `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all`. Sources HOWITWORKS 109, 113 (users must be registered first; otherwise they can't reach the resource until they register); DEPLOY 250 (enforce once users are ready).
  Note: "Users who haven't registered a phishing-resistant method are blocked from every resource once it's enforced. Get them registered first."
- Requires: `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Source DEPLOY 254-256 (all users, excluding break-glass accounts).
  Note: "Exclude the emergency access accounts from the all-users policy."
- Requires: `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts`. Source CA-ALL 94 (all-users authentication-strength policy: exclude the Directory Synchronization Accounts role under hybrid identity). DEPLOY does not repeat it, so this relies on the general all-users template.
  Note: "With Connect or Cloud Sync, exclude the Directory Synchronization Accounts role. Sync accounts can't do phishing-resistant MFA."
- RecommendedFirst: `entra.phishing-resistant-admins`. Source DEPLOY 202, 352-357.
  Note: "Learn typically starts with admins and then moves to other users, by device platform. The order can change for your organization."
- Rollout (DEPLOY 252-261, 263-271, 335-342, 389-399): "Create the all-users policy in report-only mode early, before registration campaigns, to record which sign-ins it would block." / "Enforce it in waves, one policy per device platform, for groups of users who are ready." / "Once almost every user is in a ready group, turn the all-users policy on and remove the per-platform policies."
- Verifying tests:
  - CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.1.ps1` 39-55): an enabled policy with includeUsers All, includeApplications All, and the built-in strength (id ...0004) or a custom strength limited to WHfB, FIDO2, multifactor CBA. Does not check exclusions or narrowing conditions. **Matches.** Phishing-resistant only; no "or" path.
  - ASD.ISM-1872 (`tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1872.ps1` 41): **shim** of CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 (`return Test-MtCisaPhishResistant`); same step.
  - ZTA.21784: **drop.** It accepts any strength that contains at least one phishing-resistant method (3.1.0 lines 110-131). The built-in *MFA* strength contains FIDO2, WHfB and CBA (STRENGTHS 86-90), so an all-users MFA policy passes. It also fails when any policy excludes a user (lines 147-152), so it fails a tenant that excludes break-glass accounts by user, against `entra.emergency-access-excluded`. Its title (sign-in activity) also doesn't describe its logic.
- No CIS or MT test checks phishing-resistant MFA for all users.

## Final step list (draft section 15 row)

`entra.passkeys-enabled` and `entra.temporary-access-pass` → `intune.windows-hello` (recommended after passkeys)
[+ optional `entra.certificate-based-auth`, `intune.macos-platform-sso`] → `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-admins`
(requires one method; TAP recommended first) → `entra.phishing-resistant-admins` (requires admin registration and
emergency access exclusion) → `entra.phishing-resistant-registered-all` (new, Unchecked) → `entra.phishing-resistant-all`
(requires all-user registration, emergency access and sync exclusions; admins recommended first).

Verifying tests: EIDSCA.AF01, AF02 (ZTA.21839, 21838) · EIDSCA.AT01 · unchecked (ZTA.24551) · unchecked (ZTA.21782) ·
CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 (ZTA.21783) · unchecked (ZTA.21801) · CISA.MS.AAD.3.1, ASD.ISM-1872.

## Changes to the draft, with evidence

| Draft | Change | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.windows-hello` as a link in the chain | `intune.windows-hello`, a `RequiresOneOf` member | STRENGTHS 72-76, 86-90; DEPLOY 163-170; INTUNE-PWL 128; check reads Intune |
| `entra.phishing-resistant-registered` (admins) | rename `-registered-admins`; add `-registered-all` | Draft ID suggests all users; DEPLOY 95, 250 and HOWITWORKS 113 back all-user registration before enforcement |
| EIDSCA.AF03-AF06 | no step | Optional per PASSKEY 171-178; attestation blocks synced passkeys (221), which DEPLOY 136 recommends |
| EIDSCA.AT02 | no step | TAP 86, 170-173: multiuse is the default and supported |
| CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 | no step (or name it with an explicit union rule) | 8 roles incl. Hybrid Identity Admin vs CIS 15 vs Learn 14; built-in strength only |
| ZTA.21781 | drop | Sign-in activity, UnderConstruction in 3.1.0 |
| ZTA.21784 | drop | Accepts MFA strength; fails on user exclusions |
| TAP as a sequential prerequisite | RecommendedFirst on the two registration states | TAP is one of two bootstrap paths (TAP 47-50; DEPLOY 125-127) |
| Admins before all users | RecommendedFirst, not Requires | DEPLOY 202 says "typically" and that it can change |

Test-quality notes for follow-up (not step changes): CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 matches the strength by display name, while CISA
3.1 in the same suite accepts custom strengths; ZTA.21783 counts report-only policies (its own TODO, 3.1.0 line 32).
