1	# privileged-access (Standing privilege to PIM): findings
2	
3	Mirror paths are under `scratchpad/mirrors/entra-docs-mirror/`. URLs come from each page's `canonicalUrl` front matter.
4	ZTA logic was read from the installed ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0 (`~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/ZeroTrustAssessment/3.1.0/tests/`).
5	The pack's catalog pins 2.6.0.
6	
7	## Summary of changes to the draft
8	
9	Draft: `entra.emergency-access-excluded` → `entra.pim-eligible-roles` → `entra.pim-alerts` → `entra.pim-roles-used`.
10	
11	Proposed: `entra.emergency-access-accounts` (new) → `entra.pim-activation-mfa` (new, unchecked), `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (new) and
12	`entra.pim-notifications` (the draft's `entra.pim-alerts`, renamed) → `entra.pim-eligible-roles`, which becomes the goal's `Step`.
13	
14	1. **Learn's PIM prerequisite is the emergency access *accounts* (permanent active Global Administrators), not their Conditional Access exclusion.**
15	   No PIM page links CA exclusion to PIM. Add `entra.emergency-access-accounts`. Drop `entra.emergency-access-excluded` from this chain, or keep it only
16	   through the M1 link proposed below.
17	2. **Learn puts role settings before eligible assignments.** `pim-getting-started.md` L71-77 and `pim-deployment-plan.md` L178-199 order it: role settings,
18	   then eligible assignments, then activation. The draft puts the settings-type step (`pim-alerts`) after `pim-eligible-roles`.
19	3. **CISA.MS.AAD.7.7 checks PIM notification rules, not PIM security alerts.** It reads `Notification_Admin_Admin_Eligibility` and
20	   `Notification_Admin_Admin_Assignment` and needs additional recipients on them. Rename the step to `entra.pim-notifications`. No test checks whether
21	   PIM *security alerts* are configured (`alertConfiguration.isEnabled`), so an "alerts" step would have no verifier.
22	4. **Drop `entra.pim-roles-used` from this goal.** Learn treats unused roles as a security alert to act on, with access reviews as prevention, not as a
23	   rollout step (`pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts.md` L71-82). MT.1030 also passes when nothing is eligible (the alert has nothing to fire on).
24	   As the goal's last step, it could read Done before PIM is used.
25	5. **MT.1025–MT.1028 don't verify any step in this goal** (see `entra.pim-eligible-roles` below).
26	6. **ZTA.21876 is a placeholder.** It returns "Planned for future release" with `SkippedBecause UnderConstruction`, so drop it. The draft missed
27	   ZTA.21815, the closest ZTA match.
28	7. **`OnlyWhen license:AAD_PREMIUM_P2` is wrong for PIM.** Learn says PIM needs Entra ID P2 *or* Entra ID Governance
29	   (`docs/id-governance/licensing-fundamentals.md` L213-217; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/licensing-fundamentals). The OnlyWhen
30	   grammar (`Get-MtStepCatalog.ps1` L137, `steps.schema.json` L78-82) only ANDs plans with `&`. It has no any-of, so a P1 + Governance tenant would read
31	   Not applicable. The tests already say `License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2','Entra_Identity_Governance')`. Recommendation: add any-of to the grammar, e.g.
32	   `license:AAD_PREMIUM_P2|Entra_Identity_Governance`, and use it on the four PIM steps. Until then, omit OnlyWhen and let the tests' licence gate make the
33	   step Unknown.
34	
35	## Step 1: `entra.emergency-access-accounts` (new)
36	
37	- **Title:** Keep two emergency access accounts as permanent Global Administrators
38	- **Summary:** Two cloud-only break-glass accounts can always sign in and administer the tenant, even after every other admin role is made eligible.
39	- **OnlyWhen:** none
40	- **Unchecked:** No Maester check reads the emergency accounts' Global Administrator assignment yet. ZTA.21835 checks it together with phishing-resistant
41	  sign-in and CA exclusion. (148 characters)
42	- **Sources:**
43	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access
44	    (`docs/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md`)
45	    - L66-68: create two or more cloud-only accounts and assign them Global Administrator.
46	    - L69-76: give them a passwordless method.
47	    - L91 and L122: in PIM, make their Global Administrator assignment permanent active, not eligible.
48	    - Note: "Create at least two cloud-only accounts with phishing-resistant sign-in, and give them Global Administrator as a permanent active assignment
49	      in PIM rather than an eligible one."
50	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan
51	    (`docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan.md`)
52	    - L108-110: keep zero permanent active assignments apart from the emergency access accounts, which hold Global Administrator permanently.
53	    - Note: "The emergency access accounts are the only principals PIM should leave with a permanent active role, and that role is Global Administrator."
54	- **Verifying tests:**
55	  - **ZTA.21835.** Catalog title "Emergency account exists"; the 3.1.0 title is "Emergency access accounts are configured appropriately". It finds
56	    permanent, cloud-only Global Administrator users that have a FIDO2 or certificate method and are excluded from every enabled CA policy. It passes with
57	    exactly two, fails with fewer and returns Investigate above two. It is stricter than the step because it bundles the CA exclusion and the method, which
58	    Learn's account-creation list also asks for. Acceptable as the ZTA reference.
59	  - **CIS.M365.5.3.1** tolerates up to two configured emergency accounts but does not require them, so it does not verify this step.
60	  - Suggest a new MT readiness check: "Emergency access accounts hold Global Administrator as permanent active". It would read
61	    `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` for the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting.
62	- **M1 link (proposed):** give `entra.emergency-access-excluded` `RecommendedFirst: ["entra.emergency-access-accounts"]`.
63	  - Source: security-emergency-access.md L68 (create the accounts and assign the role) comes before L77 (check the CA exclusion).
64	  - Note: "Learn's checklist creates the accounts and gives them Global Administrator before it checks that Conditional Access policies exclude them."
65	  - Side effect: the M1 goals then show this unchecked step as "Recommended first".
66	
67	## Step 2: `entra.pim-activation-mfa` (new; optional, unchecked)
68	
69	- **Title:** Require MFA to activate privileged roles in PIM
70	- **Summary:** Activating an eligible privileged role asks for multifactor authentication or a Conditional Access authentication context.
71	- **OnlyWhen:** PIM licence (see item 7 above).
72	- **Unchecked:** No check reads the PIM activation MFA rule yet. PIM's alert for roles without MFA on activation would make the step checkable.
73	- **Sources:**
74	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings (`pim-how-to-change-default-settings.md`)
75	    - L76-88: on activation, require MFA.
76	    - L90-111: or require a CA authentication context.
77	    - L109: create and turn on the CA policy for the context *before* selecting the context in PIM.
78	    - Note: "Each role can demand MFA, or a Conditional Access authentication context, at activation. Turn on the context's CA policy before you pick it
79	      in PIM."
80	  - pim-deployment-plan.md L184-188: the example settings require MFA for Global Administrator and Exchange Administrator.
81	  - pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts.md L84-93: alert "Roles don't require MFA for activation".
82	- **Rollout:** "Create and turn on the Conditional Access policy for the authentication context before you select that context in the role's PIM settings."
83	- **To make it checkable:** Graph has `noMfaOnRoleActivationAlertConfiguration`. `Test-MtPimAlertsExists` could add `NoMfaOnRoleActivationAlert` to its
84	  ValidateSet. That would be a new MT ID (issue #697). Include the step only if that check is planned.
85	
86	## Step 3: `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (new)
87	
88	- **Title:** Require approval to activate Global Administrator
89	- **Summary:** Each Global Administrator activation waits for a named approver before it takes effect.
90	- **Requires:** `entra.emergency-access-accounts`
91	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings, L146-156: approval needs at least one
92	    approver, and two are recommended. Without named approvers, active Global and Privileged Role Administrators approve. If all of them are eligible, the
93	    tenant is locked out; emergency access accounts and named approvers avoid this.
94	  - security-emergency-access.md L62 describes the same lock-out.
95	  - Note: "With approval on, no named approver and no active Global or Privileged Role Administrator, nobody can approve an activation. Permanent
96	    emergency accounts prevent the lock-out."
97	- **Source for the setting itself:** pim-deployment-plan.md L184-186. The example Global Administrator settings require approval by another Global
98	  Administrator.
99	- **Rollout:** "Name at least two approvers before you require approval." (change-default-settings L148)
100	- **Verifying tests:**
101	  - **CIS.M365.5.3.4** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.3.4.ps1`): the `Approval_EndUser_Assignment` rule has `isApprovalRequired` and at least one primary
102	    approver. **Matches** the step.
103	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.6**: the ApprovalRule `isApprovalRequired` is true; approvers are not checked. **Partial verifier.** It fails only when the step is not
104	    done, but it passes the no-approver configuration that Learn warns about.
105	  - **ZTA.21817** ("Global Administrator role activation triggers an approval workflow"): approval required with at least one primary approver.
106	    **Matches.**
107	  - **CIS.M365.5.3.5** (approval for Privileged Role Administrator): no step. Learn's example settings ask approval only for Global Administrator.
108	
109	## Step 4: `entra.pim-notifications` (draft `entra.pim-alerts`, renamed)
110	
111	- **Title:** Send PIM role notifications to a monitored mailbox
112	- **Summary:** Assignments to and activations of highly privileged roles email a security mailbox as well as the default recipients.
113	- **Sources:**
114	  - pim-how-to-change-default-settings.md L190-195 (Notifications tab: add recipients per email type).
115	    - Note: "Each role's PIM settings can copy assignment and activation emails to extra recipients, such as a security team mailbox."
116	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/best-practices, L66: notifications warn when someone is added to a highly
117	    privileged role.
118	  - security-planning.md L98 says the same.
119	- **Relationships:** none Learn-backed, apart from being a role setting (see the RecommendedFirst on step 5). Learn does not order notifications after
120	  eligible assignments.
121	- **Verifying tests** (each checks part of the step):
122	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.7**: the eligible and active assignment notification rules (`Notification_Admin_Admin_Eligibility`, `Notification_Admin_Admin_Assignment`)
123	    have `notificationRecipients` on all 8 CISA highly privileged roles.
124	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.8** and **7.9** (`Test-MtCisaActivationNotification`): the activation notification rule (`Notification_Admin_EndUser_Assignment`) has
125	    recipients, for Global Administrator (7.8) and the other 7 roles (7.9).
126	  - **ZTA.21818, ZTA.21819 and ZTA.21820** also pass when only the default recipients are on. They are laxer, so they **don't match**.
127	  - **ZTA.21899** is a placeholder (UnderConstruction).
128	
129	## Step 5: `entra.pim-eligible-roles` (the goal's `Step`)
130	
131	- **Title:** Make privileged role assignments eligible in PIM
132	- **Summary:** Administrators hold privileged roles only as eligible assignments that they activate when needed; only the emergency access accounts stay
133	  permanently active.
134	- **OnlyWhen:** PIM licence (item 7).
135	  - Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started, L53.
136	  - Note: "PIM, including eligible assignments, needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance."
137	- **Requires:** `entra.emergency-access-accounts`
138	  - security-emergency-access.md L62 and L91.
139	  - pim-deployment-plan.md L108-110.
140	  - Note: "Before making Global and Privileged Role Administrators eligible, keep emergency accounts permanently active. With every admin eligible, an
141	    approval or MFA failure can lock the tenant."
142	- **RecommendedFirst:** `entra.pim-activation-mfa`, `entra.pim-approval-global-admin`, `entra.pim-notifications`
143	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started, L71-77.
144	    - Note: "Learn's setup order for Entra roles is role settings first, then eligible assignments, then activation."
145	  - pim-deployment-plan.md L178-199.
146	    - Note: "Decide MFA, approval, notifications and activation length for each privileged role before you hand out eligible assignments."
147	- **Rollout** (pim-deployment-plan L116-122, L134, L156-158, L174; pim-security-wizard L64-77):
148	  - "Pilot with test users or a small admin group, and check that activation, approval and notifications behave as planned."
149	  - "Make Global Administrator and Security Administrator assignments eligible first, then the other privileged roles."
150	  - "Remove service principals from privileged roles, or give them time-bound active assignments; they can't be eligible."
151	  - "If activation fails in production, make the affected assignments active again, then fix the settings."
152	- **Verifying tests:**
153	  - **CIS.M365.5.3.1** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.3.1.ps1`). It reads `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` for roles with `isPrivileged`. Users and groups pass
154	    only when `Activated`. Service principals pass only with an end date. Up to two configured `EmergencyAccessAccounts` may hold permanent Global
155	    Administrator. **Matches** the step.
156	    - Caveats: it caps the emergency accounts at 2, where Learn says "two or more" (L66). It exempts only accounts listed in maester-config, so the step
157	      needs the setting.
158	  - **ASD.ISM-1649**: a **shim** of CIS.M365.5.3.1 (`return Test-MtCisPrivilegedRolesActivatedNotAssigned`). It must name the same step.
159	  - **MT.1031** (`RolesAssignedOutsidePimAlert`, Control Plane roles, emergency accounts left out): **partial.** An assignment outside PIM is standing
160	    access, so a failure means the step is not done. It passes on permanent active assignments made in PIM.
161	    - Weakness: `Test-MtPimAlertsExists` never reads `alertConfiguration.isEnabled` (L48-52, L92), so MT.1029–1032 pass when the alert is turned off.
162	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.5**: Assigned schedules with a null `createdUsing` or `startDateTime` on 8 roles. **Partial**, same reasoning as MT.1031. It has no
163	    exception for the emergency accounts, so an emergency assignment made before PIM fails it. Recommend leaving the configured accounts out, as CIS 5.3.1
164	    does.
165	  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.4**: Assigned schedules with `noExpiration` on 8 roles. It has **no exception for the emergency accounts**, so it fails in every tenant
166	    that follows Learn. Don't name the step until 7.4 leaves the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` out.
167	  - **ZTA.21815** ("activated just in time and not permanently active"): permanent privileged assignments, emergency accounts excluded. **Partial**: it
168	    accepts time-bound active. Add it.
169	  - **ZTA.21816** ("managed with PIM"): it fails when there is no eligible Global Administrator, any privileged member is outside PIM or permanent, or more
170	    than 2 users hold permanent Global Administrator. **Matches** closely. Keep it.
171	  - **ZTA.21876**: placeholder. Drop it.
172	  - **MT.1025–MT.1028: not verifiers.**
173	    - `Test-MtPrivPermanentDirectoryRole` (L53, L64-125) reads every active assignment in `roleAssignments`. It filters by principal type (guest, hybrid,
174	      service principal with a secret, mailbox) on Control Plane roles. It never reads schedules, so "permanent" in the titles is not checked.
175	    - A tenant whose Global Administrators are all permanent, cloud-only members without mailboxes passes all four, so the step would show Done wrongly.
176	      They also fail for reasons outside the step, for example a hybrid user with an eligible role.
177	    - They test admin-account hygiene: security-planning.md L165-172 (separate, cloud-only admin accounts with mail forwarded) and best-practices L122-124.
178	      That is a later goal (see "Other tests").
179	    - Separate bug: MT.1027's L86 reads `$DirectAssignments.principal | Where-Object { $_.principal.servicePrincipalType ... }`. The double `.principal`
180	      means it never finds a secret on the service principal itself.
181	
182	## Draft step `entra.pim-roles-used` (MT.1030): recommend dropping from this goal
183	
184	- MT.1030 checks `RedundantAssignmentAlert` on Control Plane roles. Learn's alert (security-alerts L71-82) fires when a user goes N days without
185	  *activating*. Its fix is removing the role; its prevention is recurring access reviews (best-practices L77-86; security-planning L250-259).
186	- It is maintenance after PIM, not a rollout step. It passes vacuously when no role is eligible. It also inherits the `isEnabled` gap above.
187	- Learn's *pre-PIM* step is "discover and remove unneeded role holders" (deployment plan L164-168; security-planning L110-121). It has no single-definition
188	  verifier: MT.1029 uses the PIM threshold, ASD.ISM-1648 uses 45 days, and GA counts are 2–8 (CISA.MS.AAD.7.1), 2–4 (CIS.M365.1.1.3) or alert-based
189	  (MT.1032).
190	- Suggest a later "privileged access hygiene" goal for MT.1029, MT.1030, ASD.ISM-1648 and CIS.M365.5.3.3 (access reviews of 6 roles, weekly or monthly).
191	  CIS.M365.5.3.3 is stricter than Learn, which allows any recurrence.
192	
193	## Other tests in `tests/` on the same data
194	
195	None of these name a step in this goal. Grouped by what they check, for later goals:
196	
197	| Concern | Tests | Notes |
198	| --- | --- | --- |
199	| Cloud-only admins | MT.1026, CISA.MS.AAD.7.3, CIS.M365.1.1.1, ZTA.21814 | Scopes differ: CISA covers Global Administrator only, MT covers Control Plane |
200	| Admin mailbox or licences | MT.1028, ASD.ISM-1175, CIS.M365.1.1.4 | ASD reads eligible assignments too |
201	| Guest admins | MT.1025, ZTA.22128 | |
202	| Workload identities in privileged roles | MT.1027, ZTA.21836; MT.1207, MT.1209 and MT.1210 for agents | |
203	| Global Administrator count and ratio | CISA.MS.AAD.7.1, CISA.MS.AAD.7.2, CIS.M365.1.1.3, MT.1032, ZTA.21812, ZTA.21813 | |
204	| Stale admins and access reviews | MT.1029, ASD.ISM-1648, CIS.M365.5.3.3, ZTA.21854 and ZTA.21855 (placeholders) | |
205	
206	- EIDSCA and ORCA read no PIM or role data.
207	- The only shim in this area is ASD.ISM-1649.
208	
209	## Final proposal
210	
211	| Step | Requires | RecommendedFirst | Verifiers |
212	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
213	| `entra.emergency-access-accounts` | — | — | Unchecked (ZTA.21835) |
214	| `entra.pim-activation-mfa` | — | — | Unchecked (needs a new check) |
215	| `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` | emergency-access-accounts | — | CIS.M365.5.3.4, CISA.MS.AAD.7.6 (partial), ZTA.21817 |
216	| `entra.pim-notifications` | — | — | CISA.MS.AAD.7.7, 7.8, 7.9 |
217	| `entra.pim-eligible-roles` (goal Step) | emergency-access-accounts | pim-activation-mfa, pim-approval-global-admin, pim-notifications | CIS.M365.5.3.1, ASD.ISM-1649 (shim), MT.1031, CISA.MS.AAD.7.5 (partial), ZTA.21815, ZTA.21816 |
218	
219	- The four PIM steps use OnlyWhen with the PIM licence: P2 or Governance, once the grammar allows any-of.
220	- Fix CISA.MS.AAD.7.4 to leave out the emergency accounts before it names `entra.pim-eligible-roles`.

The pack's catalog pins 2.6.0.

## Summary of changes to the draft

Draft: `entra.emergency-access-excluded` → `entra.pim-eligible-roles` → `entra.pim-alerts` → `entra.pim-roles-used`.

Proposed: `entra.emergency-access-accounts` (new) → `entra.pim-activation-mfa` (new, unchecked), `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (new) and
`entra.pim-notifications` (the draft's `entra.pim-alerts`, renamed) → `entra.pim-eligible-roles`, which becomes the goal's `Step`.

1. **Learn's PIM prerequisite is the emergency access *accounts* (permanent active Global Administrators), not their Conditional Access exclusion.**
   No PIM page links CA exclusion to PIM. Add `entra.emergency-access-accounts`. Drop `entra.emergency-access-excluded` from this chain, or keep it only
   through the M1 link proposed below.
2. **Learn puts role settings before eligible assignments.** `pim-getting-started.md` L71-77 and `pim-deployment-plan.md` L178-199 order it: role settings,
   then eligible assignments, then activation. The draft puts the settings-type step (`pim-alerts`) after `pim-eligible-roles`.
3. **CISA.MS.AAD.7.7 checks PIM notification rules, not PIM security alerts.** It reads `Notification_Admin_Admin_Eligibility` and
   `Notification_Admin_Admin_Assignment` and needs additional recipients on them. Rename the step to `entra.pim-notifications`. No test checks whether
   PIM *security alerts* are configured (`alertConfiguration.isEnabled`), so an "alerts" step would have no verifier.
4. **Drop `entra.pim-roles-used` from this goal.** Learn treats unused roles as a security alert to act on, with access reviews as prevention, not as a
   rollout step (`pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts.md` L71-82). MT.1030 also passes when nothing is eligible (the alert has nothing to fire on).
   As the goal's last step, it could read Done before PIM is used.
5. **MT.1025–MT.1028 don't verify any step in this goal** (see `entra.pim-eligible-roles` below).
6. **ZTA.21876 is a placeholder.** It returns "Planned for future release" with `SkippedBecause UnderConstruction`, so drop it. The draft missed
   ZTA.21815, the closest ZTA match.
7. **`OnlyWhen license:AAD_PREMIUM_P2` is wrong for PIM.** Learn says PIM needs Entra ID P2 *or* Entra ID Governance
   (`docs/id-governance/licensing-fundamentals.md` L213-217; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/licensing-fundamentals). The OnlyWhen
   grammar (`Get-MtStepCatalog.ps1` L137, `steps.schema.json` L78-82) only ANDs plans with `&`. It has no any-of, so a P1 + Governance tenant would read
   Not applicable. The tests already say `License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2','Entra_Identity_Governance')`. Recommendation: add any-of to the grammar, e.g.
   `license:AAD_PREMIUM_P2|Entra_Identity_Governance`, and use it on the four PIM steps. Until then, omit OnlyWhen and let the tests' licence gate make the
   step Unknown.

## Step 1: `entra.emergency-access-accounts` (new)

- **Title:** Keep two emergency access accounts as permanent Global Administrators
- **Summary:** Two cloud-only break-glass accounts can always sign in and administer the tenant, even after every other admin role is made eligible.
- **OnlyWhen:** none
- **Unchecked:** No Maester check reads the emergency accounts' Global Administrator assignment yet. ZTA.21835 checks it together with phishing-resistant
  sign-in and CA exclusion. (148 characters)
- **Sources:**
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access
    (`docs/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md`)
    - L66-68: create two or more cloud-only accounts and assign them Global Administrator.
    - L69-76: give them a passwordless method.
    - L91 and L122: in PIM, make their Global Administrator assignment permanent active, not eligible.
    - Note: "Create at least two cloud-only accounts with phishing-resistant sign-in, and give them Global Administrator as a permanent active assignment
      in PIM rather than an eligible one."
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan
    (`docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan.md`)
    - L108-110: keep zero permanent active assignments apart from the emergency access accounts, which hold Global Administrator permanently.
    - Note: "The emergency access accounts are the only principals PIM should leave with a permanent active role, and that role is Global Administrator."
- **Verifying tests:**
  - **ZTA.21835.** Catalog title "Emergency account exists"; the 3.1.0 title is "Emergency access accounts are configured appropriately". It finds
    permanent, cloud-only Global Administrator users that have a FIDO2 or certificate method and are excluded from every enabled CA policy. It passes with
    exactly two, fails with fewer and returns Investigate above two. It is stricter than the step because it bundles the CA exclusion and the method, which
    Learn's account-creation list also asks for. Acceptable as the ZTA reference.
  - **CIS.M365.5.3.1** tolerates up to two configured emergency accounts but does not require them, so it does not verify this step.
  - Suggest a new MT readiness check: "Emergency access accounts hold Global Administrator as permanent active". It would read
    `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` for the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` setting.
- **M1 link (proposed):** give `entra.emergency-access-excluded` `RecommendedFirst: ["entra.emergency-access-accounts"]`.
  - Source: security-emergency-access.md L68 (create the accounts and assign the role) comes before L77 (check the CA exclusion).
  - Note: "Learn's checklist creates the accounts and gives them Global Administrator before it checks that Conditional Access policies exclude them."
  - Side effect: the M1 goals then show this unchecked step as "Recommended first".

## Step 2: `entra.pim-activation-mfa` (new; optional, unchecked)

- **Title:** Require MFA to activate privileged roles in PIM
- **Summary:** Activating an eligible privileged role asks for multifactor authentication or a Conditional Access authentication context.
- **OnlyWhen:** PIM licence (see item 7 above).
- **Unchecked:** No check reads the PIM activation MFA rule yet. PIM's alert for roles without MFA on activation would make the step checkable.
- **Sources:**
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings (`pim-how-to-change-default-settings.md`)
    - L76-88: on activation, require MFA.
    - L90-111: or require a CA authentication context.
    - L109: create and turn on the CA policy for the context *before* selecting the context in PIM.
    - Note: "Each role can demand MFA, or a Conditional Access authentication context, at activation. Turn on the context's CA policy before you pick it
      in PIM."
  - pim-deployment-plan.md L184-188: the example settings require MFA for Global Administrator and Exchange Administrator.
  - pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts.md L84-93: alert "Roles don't require MFA for activation".
- **Rollout:** "Create and turn on the Conditional Access policy for the authentication context before you select that context in the role's PIM settings."
- **To make it checkable:** Graph has `noMfaOnRoleActivationAlertConfiguration`. `Test-MtPimAlertsExists` could add `NoMfaOnRoleActivationAlert` to its
  ValidateSet. That would be a new MT ID (issue #697). Include the step only if that check is planned.

## Step 3: `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (new)

- **Title:** Require approval to activate Global Administrator
- **Summary:** Each Global Administrator activation waits for a named approver before it takes effect.
- **Requires:** `entra.emergency-access-accounts`
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings, L146-156: approval needs at least one
    approver, and two are recommended. Without named approvers, active Global and Privileged Role Administrators approve. If all of them are eligible, the
    tenant is locked out; emergency access accounts and named approvers avoid this.
  - security-emergency-access.md L62 describes the same lock-out.
  - Note: "With approval on, no named approver and no active Global or Privileged Role Administrator, nobody can approve an activation. Permanent
    emergency accounts prevent the lock-out."
- **Source for the setting itself:** pim-deployment-plan.md L184-186. The example Global Administrator settings require approval by another Global
  Administrator.
- **Rollout:** "Name at least two approvers before you require approval." (change-default-settings L148)
- **Verifying tests:**
  - **CIS.M365.5.3.4** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.3.4.ps1`): the `Approval_EndUser_Assignment` rule has `isApprovalRequired` and at least one primary
    approver. **Matches** the step.
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.6**: the ApprovalRule `isApprovalRequired` is true; approvers are not checked. **Partial verifier.** It fails only when the step is not
    done, but it passes the no-approver configuration that Learn warns about.
  - **ZTA.21817** ("Global Administrator role activation triggers an approval workflow"): approval required with at least one primary approver.
    **Matches.**
  - **CIS.M365.5.3.5** (approval for Privileged Role Administrator): no step. Learn's example settings ask approval only for Global Administrator.

## Step 4: `entra.pim-notifications` (draft `entra.pim-alerts`, renamed)

- **Title:** Send PIM role notifications to a monitored mailbox
- **Summary:** Assignments to and activations of highly privileged roles email a security mailbox as well as the default recipients.
- **Sources:**
  - pim-how-to-change-default-settings.md L190-195 (Notifications tab: add recipients per email type).
    - Note: "Each role's PIM settings can copy assignment and activation emails to extra recipients, such as a security team mailbox."
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/best-practices, L66: notifications warn when someone is added to a highly
    privileged role.
  - security-planning.md L98 says the same.
- **Relationships:** none Learn-backed, apart from being a role setting (see the RecommendedFirst on step 5). Learn does not order notifications after
  eligible assignments.
- **Verifying tests** (each checks part of the step):
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.7**: the eligible and active assignment notification rules (`Notification_Admin_Admin_Eligibility`, `Notification_Admin_Admin_Assignment`)
    have `notificationRecipients` on all 8 CISA highly privileged roles.
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.8** and **7.9** (`Test-MtCisaActivationNotification`): the activation notification rule (`Notification_Admin_EndUser_Assignment`) has
    recipients, for Global Administrator (7.8) and the other 7 roles (7.9).
  - **ZTA.21818, ZTA.21819 and ZTA.21820** also pass when only the default recipients are on. They are laxer, so they **don't match**.
  - **ZTA.21899** is a placeholder (UnderConstruction).

## Step 5: `entra.pim-eligible-roles` (the goal's `Step`)

- **Title:** Make privileged role assignments eligible in PIM
- **Summary:** Administrators hold privileged roles only as eligible assignments that they activate when needed; only the emergency access accounts stay
  permanently active.
- **OnlyWhen:** PIM licence (item 7).
  - Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started, L53.
  - Note: "PIM, including eligible assignments, needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance."
- **Requires:** `entra.emergency-access-accounts`
  - security-emergency-access.md L62 and L91.
  - pim-deployment-plan.md L108-110.
  - Note: "Before making Global and Privileged Role Administrators eligible, keep emergency accounts permanently active. With every admin eligible, an
    approval or MFA failure can lock the tenant."
- **RecommendedFirst:** `entra.pim-activation-mfa`, `entra.pim-approval-global-admin`, `entra.pim-notifications`
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started, L71-77.
    - Note: "Learn's setup order for Entra roles is role settings first, then eligible assignments, then activation."
  - pim-deployment-plan.md L178-199.
    - Note: "Decide MFA, approval, notifications and activation length for each privileged role before you hand out eligible assignments."
- **Rollout** (pim-deployment-plan L116-122, L134, L156-158, L174; pim-security-wizard L64-77):
  - "Pilot with test users or a small admin group, and check that activation, approval and notifications behave as planned."
  - "Make Global Administrator and Security Administrator assignments eligible first, then the other privileged roles."
  - "Remove service principals from privileged roles, or give them time-bound active assignments; they can't be eligible."
  - "If activation fails in production, make the affected assignments active again, then fix the settings."
- **Verifying tests:**
  - **CIS.M365.5.3.1** (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.3.1.ps1`). It reads `roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` for roles with `isPrivileged`. Users and groups pass
    only when `Activated`. Service principals pass only with an end date. Up to two configured `EmergencyAccessAccounts` may hold permanent Global
    Administrator. **Matches** the step.
    - Caveats: it caps the emergency accounts at 2, where Learn says "two or more" (L66). It exempts only accounts listed in maester-config, so the step
      needs the setting.
  - **ASD.ISM-1649**: a **shim** of CIS.M365.5.3.1 (`return Test-MtCisPrivilegedRolesActivatedNotAssigned`). It must name the same step.
  - **MT.1031** (`RolesAssignedOutsidePimAlert`, Control Plane roles, emergency accounts left out): **partial.** An assignment outside PIM is standing
    access, so a failure means the step is not done. It passes on permanent active assignments made in PIM.
    - Weakness: `Test-MtPimAlertsExists` never reads `alertConfiguration.isEnabled` (L48-52, L92), so MT.1029–1032 pass when the alert is turned off.
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.5**: Assigned schedules with a null `createdUsing` or `startDateTime` on 8 roles. **Partial**, same reasoning as MT.1031. It has no
    exception for the emergency accounts, so an emergency assignment made before PIM fails it. Recommend leaving the configured accounts out, as CIS 5.3.1
    does.
  - **CISA.MS.AAD.7.4**: Assigned schedules with `noExpiration` on 8 roles. It has **no exception for the emergency accounts**, so it fails in every tenant
    that follows Learn. Don't name the step until 7.4 leaves the `EmergencyAccessAccounts` out.
  - **ZTA.21815** ("activated just in time and not permanently active"): permanent privileged assignments, emergency accounts excluded. **Partial**: it
    accepts time-bound active. Add it.
  - **ZTA.21816** ("managed with PIM"): it fails when there is no eligible Global Administrator, any privileged member is outside PIM or permanent, or more
    than 2 users hold permanent Global Administrator. **Matches** closely. Keep it.
  - **ZTA.21876**: placeholder. Drop it.
  - **MT.1025–MT.1028: not verifiers.**
    - `Test-MtPrivPermanentDirectoryRole` (L53, L64-125) reads every active assignment in `roleAssignments`. It filters by principal type (guest, hybrid,
      service principal with a secret, mailbox) on Control Plane roles. It never reads schedules, so "permanent" in the titles is not checked.
    - A tenant whose Global Administrators are all permanent, cloud-only members without mailboxes passes all four, so the step would show Done wrongly.
      They also fail for reasons outside the step, for example a hybrid user with an eligible role.
    - They test admin-account hygiene: security-planning.md L165-172 (separate, cloud-only admin accounts with mail forwarded) and best-practices L122-124.
      That is a later goal (see "Other tests").
    - Separate bug: MT.1027's L86 reads `$DirectAssignments.principal | Where-Object { $_.principal.servicePrincipalType ... }`. The double `.principal`
      means it never finds a secret on the service principal itself.

## Draft step `entra.pim-roles-used` (MT.1030): recommend dropping from this goal

- MT.1030 checks `RedundantAssignmentAlert` on Control Plane roles. Learn's alert (security-alerts L71-82) fires when a user goes N days without
  *activating*. Its fix is removing the role; its prevention is recurring access reviews (best-practices L77-86; security-planning L250-259).
- It is maintenance after PIM, not a rollout step. It passes vacuously when no role is eligible. It also inherits the `isEnabled` gap above.
- Learn's *pre-PIM* step is "discover and remove unneeded role holders" (deployment plan L164-168; security-planning L110-121). It has no single-definition
  verifier: MT.1029 uses the PIM threshold, ASD.ISM-1648 uses 45 days, and GA counts are 2–8 (CISA.MS.AAD.7.1), 2–4 (CIS.M365.1.1.3) or alert-based
  (MT.1032).
- Suggest a later "privileged access hygiene" goal for MT.1029, MT.1030, ASD.ISM-1648 and CIS.M365.5.3.3 (access reviews of 6 roles, weekly or monthly).
  CIS.M365.5.3.3 is stricter than Learn, which allows any recurrence.

## Other tests in `tests/` on the same data

None of these name a step in this goal. Grouped by what they check, for later goals:

| Concern | Tests | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloud-only admins | MT.1026, CISA.MS.AAD.7.3, CIS.M365.1.1.1, ZTA.21814 | Scopes differ: CISA covers Global Administrator only, MT covers Control Plane |
| Admin mailbox or licences | MT.1028, ASD.ISM-1175, CIS.M365.1.1.4 | ASD reads eligible assignments too |
| Guest admins | MT.1025, ZTA.22128 | |
| Workload identities in privileged roles | MT.1027, ZTA.21836; MT.1207, MT.1209 and MT.1210 for agents | |
| Global Administrator count and ratio | CISA.MS.AAD.7.1, CISA.MS.AAD.7.2, CIS.M365.1.1.3, MT.1032, ZTA.21812, ZTA.21813 | |
| Stale admins and access reviews | MT.1029, ASD.ISM-1648, CIS.M365.5.3.3, ZTA.21854 and ZTA.21855 (placeholders) | |

- EIDSCA and ORCA read no PIM or role data.
- The only shim in this area is ASD.ISM-1649.

## Final proposal

| Step | Requires | RecommendedFirst | Verifiers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.emergency-access-accounts` | — | — | Unchecked (ZTA.21835) |
| `entra.pim-activation-mfa` | — | — | Unchecked (needs a new check) |
| `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` | emergency-access-accounts | — | CIS.M365.5.3.4, CISA.MS.AAD.7.6 (partial), ZTA.21817 |
| `entra.pim-notifications` | — | — | CISA.MS.AAD.7.7, 7.8, 7.9 |
| `entra.pim-eligible-roles` (goal Step) | emergency-access-accounts | pim-activation-mfa, pim-approval-global-admin, pim-notifications | CIS.M365.5.3.1, ASD.ISM-1649 (shim), MT.1031, CISA.MS.AAD.7.5 (partial), ZTA.21815, ZTA.21816 |

- The four PIM steps use OnlyWhen with the PIM licence: P2 or Governance, once the grammar allows any-of.
- Fix CISA.MS.AAD.7.4 to leave out the emergency accounts before it names `entra.pim-eligible-roles`.
- `entra.emergency-access-excluded` stays in Foundation and gains RecommendedFirst `entra.emergency-access-accounts`.

1	# Goal `email-authentication`: findings (M2 expert pass)
2	
3	Mirror root: `defender-docs-mirror/defender-office-365/`. Short names below:
4	ABOUT = `email-authentication-about.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-about),
5	SPF = `email-authentication-spf-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-spf-configure),
6	DKIM = `email-authentication-dkim-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-dkim-configure),
7	DMARC = `email-authentication-dmarc-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-dmarc-configure),
8	GUIDE = `mdo-deployment-guide.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/mdo-deployment-guide).
9	All canonical URLs confirmed from the pages' front matter (ms.date 2026-07-03). The exchange-docs-mirror has no
10	page that orders SPF, DKIM and DMARC; it is not needed.
11	
12	## Summary of changes to the draft
13	
14	| Draft | Recommended | Why |
15	| --- | --- | --- |
16	| product key `exchange` | `defender` (owner's call; `exchange` also valid) | See "Product key" below |
17	| `exchange.spf`: CIS 2.1.8, CISA 2.2, ORCA.235 | `defender.spf`: CIS 2.1.8, CISA 2.2 | ORCA.235 fails `~all`; CIS 2.1.8 accepts it. Stricter, so its own step |
18	| (none) | new `defender.spf-hard-fail`: ORCA.235 | Learn recommends `-all` once all senders are known |
19	| `exchange.dkim`: 4 tests | `defender.dkim`: same 4 tests | All four match |
20	| `exchange.dmarc-monitor`: CIS 2.1.10, CISA 4.1, 4.3 | `defender.dmarc-published`: CISA 4.1 only | CIS 2.1.10 needs quarantine/reject plus rua and ruf. CISA 4.3 is CISA's own address. CISA 4.1 checks only that a record exists, so "monitor" overstates it |
21	| (none) | `defender.dmarc-enforce`, redefined: CIS 2.1.10 | quarantine or reject, pct 100, rua and ruf on every domain: GUIDE's definition |
22	| `exchange.dmarc-enforce`: CISA 4.2, MT.1182 | `defender.dmarc-reject`: CISA 4.2, MT.1182 (goal step) | Both need p=reject |

24	
25	The draft ID `dmarc-enforce` gets a new meaning here. If that is confusing, name CIS 2.1.10's step
26	`defender.dmarc-quarantine` and keep the rest. No step is Unchecked. No ZTA test covers SPF, DKIM or DMARC.
27	
28	## Product key
29	
30	Product declared today: CIS 2.1.8, 2.1.9, 2.1.10 and ORCA.235, 108, 108.1 = `defender` (2.1.9 and the ORCA tests have
31	RelatedProduct `exchange`). CISA 2.2, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 = `exchange` (3.1 has RelatedProduct `defender`). MT.1182 = `entra`.
32	The taxonomy has `email-authentication` under both `exchange` and `defender`
33	(`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` lines 53, 80).
34	
35	Recommend `defender`:
36	- The rubric says Product is "the product whose admin surface holds the setting" (`attribute-rubric.md` line 40).
37	  The only Microsoft 365 surface for any of these steps is the Defender portal's Email authentication settings page
38	  (DKIM lines 207-209). SPF and DMARC have no portal or cmdlet (SPF line 84, DMARC line 99). The exception is the
39	  onmicrosoft.com DMARC record, which is added in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Learn files all of it under
40	  Defender for Office 365.
41	- The CIS and ORCA tests could have chosen either product, and they chose `defender`. The CISA tests say `exchange`
42	  because of the folder rule ("tests in `tests/cisa/exchange` use that folder's product", line 41). MT.1182 says
43	  `entra` for the same reason.
44	- The argument for `exchange`: the objects are Exchange Online's (`Get-AcceptedDomain`, `Get-DkimSigningConfig`), and
45	  the feature comes with every Exchange Online org without a Defender licence. If the owner prefers `exchange`, only
46	  the IDs and the file name change.
47	
48	## Steps, in order
49	
50	### 1. `defender.spf`: Publish an SPF record for every domain that sends mail
51	Summary: Receiving servers can check that mail from your domains comes from Microsoft 365 or another sender you list.
52	- Relationships: none.
53	- Source (definition): SPF lines 60-63, 112-144, 154-173, parked 73 and 174-193. Note: "Each custom domain and sending
54	  subdomain needs one SPF TXT record naming Microsoft 365 and any other senders. onmicrosoft.com is covered; parked
55	  domains get v=spf1 -all." (169 chars)
56	- Rollout (ABOUT lines 283-298; SPF lines 144, 218-229):
57	  1. List every system that sends as the domain: Microsoft 365, on-premises servers and third-party services.
58	  2. Publish one SPF TXT record per sending domain and subdomain, and keep it under ten DNS lookups.
59	  3. Give domains that never send mail the record v=spf1 -all.
60	- Tests:
61	  - CIS.M365.2.1.8 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.2.1.8.ps1` 37-118). Every custom accepted domain (the initial and
62	    coexistence domains are excluded; parked domains are included) has an SPF record whose `all` term, after any
63	    redirect, is `-all` or `~all`. **Matches.**
64	  - CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 (`tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.2.2.ps1` 37-89). Every domain with sending enabled,
65	    including the initial domain, has an SPF record whose includes, nested ones too, contain
66	    `spf.protection.outlook.com` or `outlook.com`. It does not check the `all` qualifier. **Shares the step, but checks
67	    a different part of the record.** This is CISA v1 logic. The current upstream text, MS.EXO.2.2v3, is "...fails
68	    all non-approved senders" and accepts either -all or ~all (ScubaGear `baselines/exo.md` lines 132-142). That is
69	    exactly what CIS 2.1.8 checks, so the CISA test should become a shim of `Test-MtCisSpfRecordsPublished`
70	    (AGENTS.md duplicate rule). It probably also fails GCC High, DoD and 21Vianet tenants, whose include is
71	    `spf.protection.office365.us` or `.partner.outlook.cn` (SPF lines 163-172). Verify this before relying on it.
72	
73	### 2. `defender.spf-hard-fail` (new): End every SPF record with -all
74	Summary: Receivers are told to reject mail from servers the SPF record does not list, so DMARC can act on unsigned spoofed mail.
75	- RecommendedFirst `defender.spf`: ABOUT lines 283-298. Start with the senders you know and ~all, find the rest,
76	  then switch to -all. Note: "Publish the known senders with ~all first and add the rest as you find them. A hard
77	  fail before then would bounce mail from a sender you missed." (144 chars)
78	- RecommendedFirst `defender.dmarc-published`: SPF lines 76-78 and 130-134. DMARC reports are the main way to find
79	  sources and SPF failures, and in complex organizations a p=none DMARC record should go in early. Note: "DMARC
80	  aggregate reports reveal which servers send as the domain, so read them before -all rejects a source nobody
81	  listed." (121 chars)
82	- Rollout:

# Goal `email-authentication`: findings (M2 expert pass)

Mirror root: `defender-docs-mirror/defender-office-365/`. Short names below:
ABOUT = `email-authentication-about.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-about),
SPF = `email-authentication-spf-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-spf-configure),
DKIM = `email-authentication-dkim-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-dkim-configure),
DMARC = `email-authentication-dmarc-configure.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/email-authentication-dmarc-configure),
GUIDE = `mdo-deployment-guide.md` (https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/mdo-deployment-guide).
All canonical URLs confirmed from the pages' front matter (ms.date 2026-07-03). The exchange-docs-mirror has no
page that orders SPF, DKIM and DMARC; it is not needed.

## Summary of changes to the draft

| Draft | Recommended | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| product key `exchange` | `defender` (owner's call; `exchange` also valid) | See "Product key" below |
| `exchange.spf`: CIS 2.1.8, CISA 2.2, ORCA.235 | `defender.spf`: CIS 2.1.8, CISA 2.2 | ORCA.235 fails `~all`; CIS 2.1.8 accepts it. Stricter, so its own step |
| (none) | new `defender.spf-hard-fail`: ORCA.235 | Learn recommends `-all` once all senders are known |
| `exchange.dkim`: 4 tests | `defender.dkim`: same 4 tests | All four match |
| `exchange.dmarc-monitor`: CIS 2.1.10, CISA 4.1, 4.3 | `defender.dmarc-published`: CISA 4.1 only | CIS 2.1.10 needs quarantine/reject plus rua and ruf. CISA 4.3 is CISA's own address. CISA 4.1 checks only that a record exists, so "monitor" overstates it |
| (none) | `defender.dmarc-enforce`, redefined: CIS 2.1.10 | quarantine or reject, pct 100, rua and ruf on every domain: GUIDE's definition |
| `exchange.dmarc-enforce`: CISA 4.2, MT.1182 | `defender.dmarc-reject`: CISA 4.2, MT.1182 (goal step) | Both need p=reject |
| SPF/DKIM → DMARC as hard order | Requires only on the enforcing steps, RecommendedFirst on `dmarc-published` | p=none changes no delivery. Learn even advises publishing it early to find senders |

The draft ID `dmarc-enforce` gets a new meaning here. If that is confusing, name CIS 2.1.10's step
`defender.dmarc-quarantine` and keep the rest. No step is Unchecked. No ZTA test covers SPF, DKIM or DMARC.

## Product key

Product declared today: CIS 2.1.8, 2.1.9, 2.1.10 and ORCA.235, 108, 108.1 = `defender` (2.1.9 and the ORCA tests have
RelatedProduct `exchange`). CISA 2.2, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 = `exchange` (3.1 has RelatedProduct `defender`). MT.1182 = `entra`.
The taxonomy has `email-authentication` under both `exchange` and `defender`
(`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` lines 53, 80).

- The rubric says Product is "the product whose admin surface holds the setting" (`attribute-rubric.md` line 40).
  The only Microsoft 365 surface for any of these steps is the Defender portal's Email authentication settings page
  (DKIM lines 207-209). SPF and DMARC have no portal or cmdlet (SPF line 84, DMARC line 99). The exception is the
  onmicrosoft.com DMARC record, which is added in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Learn files all of it under
  Defender for Office 365.
- The CIS and ORCA tests could have chosen either product, and they chose `defender`. The CISA tests say `exchange`
  because of the folder rule ("tests in `tests/cisa/exchange` use that folder's product", line 41). MT.1182 says
  `entra` for the same reason.
- The argument for `exchange`: the objects are Exchange Online's (`Get-AcceptedDomain`, `Get-DkimSigningConfig`), and
  the feature comes with every Exchange Online org without a Defender licence. If the owner prefers `exchange`, only
  the IDs and the file name change.

### 1. `defender.spf`: Publish an SPF record for every domain that sends mail

- Rollout (DMARC lines 193-216 and 226):
  1. Start with a low-volume domain or subdomain and leave the parent domain for last.
  2. Move from p=none to p=quarantine and raise pct in steps from 10 to 100 while you watch the reports.
  3. Keep rua and ruf addresses in the record so failures go on being reported.
- Tests: CIS.M365.2.1.10 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.2.1.10.ps1` 38-92). Every accepted domain except the coexistence
  domain, onmicrosoft.com included, has a valid DMARC record. The record is found at the domain or its organizational
  domain, and the organizational domain's `sp=` applies when the record is inherited. Its policy must be quarantine or
  reject, pct must be 100 or absent, and it must have mailto rua and ruf. **Matches.** The test title says
  "published", but p=none fails, so the draft had it under the wrong step.

### 6. `defender.dmarc-reject` (rename of the draft `dmarc-enforce`; goal step): Reject mail that fails DMARC on every domain
Summary: Receivers reject mail that claims to come from your domains but fails DMARC, parked domains and onmicrosoft.com included.
- Requires `defender.spf` and `defender.dkim`: same lines as step 5. Note: "p=reject makes receivers refuse mail
  that fails both aligned SPF and DKIM, so every sending domain needs both in place before you switch." (137 chars)
- RecommendedFirst `defender.dmarc-enforce`: DMARC lines 202-225. Note: "Each domain sits at p=quarantine and is
  watched before p=reject, so false positives land in junk folders instead of bouncing." (125 chars)
- Source (definition): DMARC line 191 (the target is p=reject for all custom domains and subdomains), lines 233-245
  (parked domains and an unused onmicrosoft.com domain get p=reject) and line 174. Note: "The end state is p=reject
  everywhere. Parked domains and an onmicrosoft.com domain that sends nothing can go straight to it." (124 chars)
- Rollout (DMARC lines 217-231):
  1. After a period at p=quarantine, move each domain to p=reject, raising pct in steps if needed.
  2. Do the subdomains in order of volume, then the parent domain.
  3. Set parked domains and an unused onmicrosoft.com domain to p=reject straight away.
- Tests (they share the step; each covers part of it, and a tenant at Learn's end state passes both, apart from the CISA 4.2 inheritance bug below):
  - CISA.MS.EXO.4.2 (`tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.4.2.ps1`). Every accepted domain except the coexistence
    domain, initial domain included, has `p=reject` in its own `_dmarc.<domain>` record. With `-Strict`, its
    second-level domain does too. pct is not checked. Bug: it does not follow inheritance, because
    `ConvertFrom-MailAuthenticationRecordDmarc` has no parent fallback, so an accepted subdomain that relies on its
    parent's p=reject fails. Learn allows relying on the parent record (DMARC line 231). Its subdomain-policy branch
    can't be reached either. Fix: use `Find-MtDmarcRecord`, as 4.1 does.
  - MT.1182 (`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1182.ps1` 50-141). For each verified, *Managed* Entra domain, the
    registrable domain has `p=reject` and pct 100. The initial domain is skipped. Narrower: it never checks
    onmicrosoft.com, it skips federated domains for no email reason, and it ignores `sp=`. It also runs on Graph
    alone, which is useful when Exchange Online isn't connected. Aside: `Product = 'entra'` and
    `Feature = 'user-settings'` don't fit a DMARC check; the rubric wants the same feature as the other DMARC tests
    (`email-authentication`).

## Goal

`email-authentication`, "Authenticate mail from your domains". Summary: "Receivers can tell real mail from your domains
from spoofed mail, and reject the spoofed mail." Step `defender.dmarc-reject`. Its steps are dmarc-reject, dmarc-enforce,
dmarc-published, spf-hard-fail, spf and dkim. The graph has no cycle, and no step names the same step in two
relationships.

## Other tests found (search of tests/ and packs/ for DMARC, DKIM, SPF, DkimSigningConfig, Resolve-DnsName, Get-MailAuthenticationRecord)

- CIS.M365.2.1.7 (HonorDmarcPolicy in anti-phishing) and ORCA.244: how inbound mail that fails DMARC is handled. A
  different setting, so no step here. They are candidates for a later Defender for Office 365 goal.
- ORCA.102: Advanced Spam Filter options, including the SPF hard-fail one (inbound). A different setting.
- ORCA.243: ARC trusted sealers when MX doesn't point to EOP. GUIDE line 92 says this is "if necessary", and no
  `OnlyWhen` condition can express it. No step.
- CISA.MS.EXO.2.1 is deprecated and always skipped. No step.
- ASD: no email tests. `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json` has ISM-0574 and ISM-1151 (SPF), ISM-0861, ISM-1026 and
  ISM-1027 (DKIM), and ISM-1540 and ISM-1799 (DMARC). Any future ASD test for these should be a shim of the tests above.
- ZTA: no SPF, DKIM or DMARC test in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/catalog.json`. ZTA.41033 covers anti-phishing
  spoof protection and is not a step here.
- No test in the set is a shim today.

## Bugs to raise separately (they don't block tagging)

1. CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 still runs the v1 logic and title. It should be the v3 shim of CIS.M365.2.1.8 (accepting -all or
   ~all). Until then it probably fails GCC High and 21Vianet SPF includes.
2. CISA.MS.EXO.4.2 doesn't follow DMARC inheritance, and its subdomain-policy branch can't be reached.
3. CISA.MS.EXO.4.3's `$checkTarget` checks the wrong variable, and the Targets column shows ruf instead of rua.
4. MT.1182 skips federated domains, and its Product and Feature don't fit the rubric.

1	# Goal `defender-device-risk`: Defender risk in compliance (M2 expert pass)
2	
3	Mirrors read 2026-11-05. Line numbers are file lines in the mirror. All URLs below were fetched and return 200.
4	
5	## Summary of changes to the draft
6	
7	1. **The order is reversed.** Learn connects the services first and onboards devices second. The draft has
8	   `defender.endpoint-onboarding` → `intune.defender-connector`; it should be connector → onboarding.
9	2. **Add a missing step**, `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`: the per-platform "Compliance policy
10	   evaluation" toggles in the connector. Learn treats it as a separate step after the connection, and the risk rule
11	   doesn't read Defender data on a platform until its toggle is on. ZTA.24871 checks this toggle (Android only),
12	   not the connection.
13	3. **MT.1098 does not verify the connector.** It skips when no connectors exist and passes when another vendor's
14	   connector is healthy and Defender's is missing. It verifies none of this goal's steps.
15	4. **Of the three draft verifying tests, only MT.1231 fits `intune.compliance-device-risk`.** MT.1235 reads a
16	   different setting (the third-party MTD "Device Threat Level" on Android device administrator). MT.1216 reads a
17	   macOS property, but Learn documents no macOS machine-risk compliance setting. Windows is the platform both
18	   Learn walkthroughs are built around, and no test checks it.
19	5. `intune.compliance-device-risk` → `intune.compliance-policies` should be **RecommendedFirst**, not Requires.
20	6. The goal's `Step` is `intune.compliance-device-risk`. The Conditional Access link is made through the goal
21	   order and the Summary, not through a relationship (see "Goal" below).
22	
23	Final order: `intune.defender-connector` → `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation` (requires the connector) and
24	`defender.endpoint-onboarding` (connector recommended first) → `intune.compliance-device-risk` (requires the
25	evaluation toggles; onboarding and `intune.compliance-policies` recommended first).
26	
27	## Step 1. `intune.defender-connector` (keep the ID; it moves to first)
28	
29	- **Title:** Connect Defender for Endpoint to Intune
30	- **Summary:** Defender for Endpoint and Intune share device data, so Intune can receive the risk level
31	  Defender gives each device.
32	- **Relationships:** none. Learn calls it a one-time setup per tenant with no Maester-side prerequisite.
33	- **Sources**
34	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration
35	    (intune-docs-mirror, `intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration.md` L78-111). The
36	    Intune page shows Connection status Unavailable until the Intune connection toggle is set to On in the Defender
37	    portal under Advanced features. It then shows Enabled, which can take up to 15 minutes.
38	    **Note:** "Turn on the Intune connection in the Defender portal's advanced features, then check that Intune
39	    reports the connection as enabled. The status can lag by about 15 minutes."
40	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/advanced-features (defender-docs-mirror,
41	    `defender-endpoint/advanced-features.md` L208-220). The integration has to be enabled in both products, and it
42	    needs Intune-managed Windows devices that are Entra joined.
43	    **Note:** "The integration must be switched on in both Defender for Endpoint and Intune before Intune can use
44	    Defender's device data."
45	- **Rollout:** none. It is a tenant toggle with no staged option.
46	- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. MT.1098 reports connector health but skips or passes when the
47	  Defender connector is missing."
48	- **New check proposed** (reserve an MT ID on #697): GET `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` (beta).
49	  Pass when the connector `fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92` (Defender for Endpoint, the ID MT.1098 L55 and
50	  ZTA.24871 already use) exists with `partnerState = enabled`. It shares the cache with MT.1098.
51	
52	## Step 2 (new). `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`
53	
54	- **Title:** Turn on compliance evaluation in the Defender for Endpoint connector
55	- **Summary:** Compliance policies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS and Android include the risk level that Defender for
56	  Endpoint reports for those devices.
57	- **Requires `intune.defender-connector`**
58	  - configure-integration.md L113-130: after the connection exists, enable "Connect Android / iOS/iPadOS / Windows
59	    devices to Defender for Endpoint" under Compliance policy evaluation. L130: this connects every applicable
60	    managed device, and future enrollments, for compliance evaluation.
61	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access (defender-docs-mirror,
62	    `defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access.md` L81-94). Step 1 is the connection. Step 2 checks that the
63	    connection is Enabled and that the Windows compliance-evaluation toggle is On.
64	  - **Note:** "Once the connection shows Enabled, turn on compliance policy evaluation for each platform in the
65	    connector settings. Each platform has its own toggle."
66	- **Rollout:** none. The toggle applies to every managed device on the platform at once (L130).
67	- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.24871 is narrower (Android only; see the tests section). No Maester test.
68	- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks Android only (ZTA.24871)."
69	  A Maester check could read `windowsEnabled`, `iosEnabled` and `androidEnabled` on the same connector record
70	  (properties confirmed in the Graph `mobileThreatDefenseConnector` schema). It would require each toggle for the
71	  platforms that have a compliance policy.
72	- Merging steps 1 and 2 into one step is possible if the owner wants fewer steps. In that case one new check must
73	  test both conditions, and ZTA.24871 still stays off the step because it covers Android only. I recommend two
74	  steps: Learn numbers them separately, and they are done in different portals with different roles
75	  (configure-integration.md L82-85 compared with L117).
76	
77	## Step 3. `defender.endpoint-onboarding` (keep the ID; it moves after the connector)
78	
79	- **Title:** Eligible devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. This is a state title, because its only test
80	  (ZTA.41045) measures coverage.
81	- **Summary:** Every device that Defender for Endpoint can protect reports to it through a working sensor, so the
82	  device has a risk level.
83	- **RecommendedFirst `intune.defender-connector`** (not Requires)
84	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager (defender-docs-mirror,
85	    `defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager.md` L63-68): the Intune-to-Defender connection is listed as a
86	    prerequisite for onboarding Windows devices with Intune.
87	  - configure-integration.md L171-175: the connection gives Intune the onboarding package automatically.
88	    L229-232 and L246-248: without the connection, the EDR policy accepts only a pasted onboarding blob. So
89	    onboarding still works without the connection, which is why this is RecommendedFirst. Other onboarding
90	    methods also exist (`defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-mdm.md`, "Onboard devices using Microsoft Intune").
91	  - Intune overview https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview
92	    (`intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview.md` L61-62): the connection is step 1 and onboarding
93	    with Intune policy is step 2.
94	  - **Note:** "Connect the services first. Intune then receives Defender's onboarding package for its EDR policy,
95	    and without the connection you must paste an onboarding blob yourself."
96	- **Rollout**
97	  - "Assign an Intune EDR onboarding policy to a test device group, and check that the devices appear in the
98	    Defender portal's device inventory." (onboarding-endpoint-manager.md L75-92; configure-integration.md
99	    L260-263)
100	  - "Then assign it to all Windows devices, or deploy the preconfigured policy that targets all devices."
101	    (configure-integration.md L183-208)
102	  - "Deploy the Defender app to macOS, Android and iOS/iPadOS devices. Intune has no automatic onboarding package
103	    for those platforms." (configure-integration.md L164-167, L269-306)
104	- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.41045 matches (see below). No Maester test.
105	- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.41045) once its
106	  results can name steps."
107	- `OnlyWhen`: the step needs Defender for Endpoint P1, P2 or Business (`MDE_LITE`, `WINDEFATP`, `MDE_SMB`).
108	  `OnlyWhen` can't express "any one of", so leave it empty and rely on each test's `License` gate. This is worth
109	  a line in section 4.4 of the design.
110	
111	## Step 4. `intune.compliance-device-risk` (keep the ID)
112	
113	- **Title:** Require a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score in compliance policies
114	- **Summary:** Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates above the allowed risk level are marked noncompliant.
115	- **Requires `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`**
116	  - configure-conditional-access.md L89-110: Step 2 (connection Enabled, platform toggle On) comes before Step 3
117	    (compliance policy with "Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score").
118	  - https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/mobile-threat-defense/enable-connector
119	    (`intune/device-security/mobile-threat-defense/enable-connector.md` L90-91): a platform's compliance policies
120	    include the connector's data only while that platform's toggle is on.
121	  - **Note:** "The risk rule reads Defender data for a platform only after that platform's compliance-evaluation
122	    toggle is turned on in the connector."
123	- **RecommendedFirst `defender.endpoint-onboarding`**
124	  - overview.md L61-63: onboarding (step 2) comes before the compliance policy (step 3).
125	  - configure-conditional-access.md L53 and L65: the setup applies to devices that are onboarded to Defender for
126	    Endpoint.
127	  - enable-connector.md L164: where possible, deploy the threat defense app before the compliance and Conditional
128	    Access rules.
129	  - Why RecommendedFirst: ZTA.41045 demands 100% coverage, and Requires would block the step until every device is
130	    onboarded.
131	  - **Note:** "Onboard devices before adding the risk rule. Only onboarded devices report a risk level, and phones
132	    need the Defender app installed before the rule applies."
133	- **RecommendedFirst `intune.compliance-policies`** (the draft had Requires)
134	  - configure-integration.md L351-353: points people who are new to compliance policies to the general
135	    create-policy guide first.
136	  - The risk score is one setting inside a platform policy. Requiring every platform to be covered first (the M1
137	    step's definition) would block a tenant that has a Windows policy but no Android Enterprise policy. Nothing on
138	    Learn says the risk rule fails without that coverage.
139	  - **Note:** "The machine risk score is a setting in each platform's compliance policy. Set up the compliance
140	    policies themselves before adding it."
141	- **Source for the Conditional Access link** (this is not a relationship). overview.md L116-118, and
142	  https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/conditional-access (`defender-endpoint/conditional-access.md`
143	  L58-62): Intune marks the risky device noncompliant, and Conditional Access does the blocking.
144	  configure-conditional-access.md L112-127 (Step 4) uses the policy-all-users-device-compliance policy, which is
145	  `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`.
146	  **Note:** "A device marked noncompliant for risk loses access only where a Conditional Access policy requires a
147	  compliant device."
148	- **Rollout**
149	  - "Set the threshold to Low, the level Learn suggests for most organizations. High blocks nothing and only
150	    reports." (configure-integration.md L374-401)
151	  - "Assign the policy to a test group and confirm its devices report the expected compliance state."
152	    (configure-conditional-access.md L108-110)
153	  - "Widen the assignment. If a compliant-device policy is already on, risky devices lose access as soon as they
154	    are marked noncompliant." (configure-integration.md L343)
155	
156	### One step or one per platform
157	
158	Use **one step**, named by one test per platform, for these reasons:
159	
160	- Learn gives one procedure with a platform choice: configure-integration.md L341-410 with the platform list at
161	  L358-363, and the "Runtime defenses" row of https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3
162	  (`intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3.md` L253).
163	- A goal has one `Step`, and per-platform steps would split it.
164	- Under "any failing test means Not done", the failing test already names the platform that is missing.
165	
166	This holds only under two conditions:
167	
168	1. **A Windows check must exist before tagging.** Both Learn walkthroughs center on Windows
169	   (configure-conditional-access.md L53 and L96-101). With MT.1231 alone the step would show Done for a tenant that
170	   protects only iPhones. Proposed check: an assigned `#microsoft.graph.windows10CompliancePolicy` with
171	   `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled = true` and `deviceThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` in secured, low or
172	   medium. On Windows the machine-risk rule is the only threat setting (ref-windows-settings.md L267-281), and the
173	   Graph type has no `advancedThreatProtection*` property. An Android Enterprise check is also needed
174	   (`advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` on `androidWorkProfileCompliancePolicy` and
175	   `androidDeviceOwnerCompliancePolicy`; ref-android-enterprise-settings.md L78-82 and L207-209).
176	2. **A platform with no compliance policy should make its test Not applicable, not a failure.** Today MT.1231
177	   (L78-84) and MT.1216 (L63-69) return `$false` when the platform has no compliance policy, so a Windows-only
178	   tenant could never complete the step. A missing policy belongs to `intune.compliance-policies`. This needs a
179	   test change (a skip with NotApplicable), and the test's owner should agree to it.
180	
181	Until both conditions hold, tag MT.1231 only. Leave the step's status partial and say so in the PR.
182	
183	## Goal
184	
185	```json
186	{ "Id": "defender-device-risk", "Title": "Block devices Defender finds at risk",
187	  "Summary": "Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates as risky become noncompliant, so the compliant-device Conditional Access policy blocks them.",
188	  "Step": "intune.compliance-device-risk" }
189	```
190	
191	Don't add `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` → RecommendedFirst `intune.compliance-device-risk`. It would pull the
192	whole Defender chain into the `compliant-devices` goal, and Learn's CA page (policy-all-users-device-compliance)
193	doesn't back it. The reverse relationship would contradict Learn's order: configure-conditional-access.md L110 says
194	to validate the compliance policy before configuring CA. List this goal after `compliant-devices` in `goals.json`.
195	If the report should show "leads to: Require compliant devices", that is a new display feature for M3/M4, not a
196	relationship. The current title, "Defender risk in compliance", is fine too. The suggested title names the outcome.
197	
198	## Verifying tests (all read)
199	
200	| Test | Definition of done (from the .ps1) | Verdict |
201	| --- | --- | --- |
202	| MT.1098 `tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1098.ps1` | Every connector returned by `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` has `partnerState = enabled` and a heartbeat no older than 1 day (L81-87). It skips when the list is empty (L63-65, L88-89). | **Doesn't verify `intune.defender-connector`.** A missing Defender connector gives Skip (no connectors at all) or Pass (another vendor's connector is healthy). It fails only for a connector that is listed and unhealthy. Learn documents an Unavailable status before connection (configure-integration.md L92) but not whether Graph lists that record, so a failure can't be relied on either. It checks the health of any vendor's connector. enable-connector.md L160 backs that this matters: Intune ignores compliance data from an unresponsive partner. It fits no step in this goal, so name **no step**. A state step "Threat defense connectors are responsive" could come later. |
203	| ZTA.24871 (pack catalog L3327; installed ZeroTrustAssessment 3.1.0 `tests/Test-Assessment.24871.ps1` L38-55) | The Defender connector exists, `partnerState = enabled` and `androidEnabled = true`. | Its title ("Defender for Endpoint automatic enrollment is enforced to reduce risk from unmanaged Android threats") names onboarding, but its logic tests the **Android compliance-evaluation toggle**. It is stricter than step 1 and narrower (Android) than step 2. Record it in step 2's Unchecked note as "Android only". Taxonomy on `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping`: intune, tenant-administration, AlsoCheckedBy []. |
204	| ZTA.41045 (catalog L5998; installed module `tests/Test-Assessment.41045.ps1`) | Advanced hunting `DeviceInfo` over 30 days, latest row per device. It fails if any device is "Can be onboarded" or is onboarded with a sensor that isn't Active, and returns Investigate when no data comes back. "Unsupported" and "Insufficient info" devices are out of scope. | **Matches** step 3. Title "All eligible endpoints are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint" fits. Licences WINDEFATP, MDE_LITE. |
205	| MT.1231 `Test.MT.1231.ps1` (helper `Get-MtMobileCompliancePolicy`, L126) | At least one assigned `iosCompliancePolicy` has `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` in secured, low or medium (L89-103). High doesn't count, which matches configure-integration.md L393-397. **It fails when there is no iOS policy** (L78-84). | **Matches for iOS**, narrower by platform. Name `intune.compliance-device-risk` once the no-policy case is changed to Not applicable (condition 2). |
206	| MT.1216 `Test.MT.1216.ps1` (helper `Get-MtMacOSCompliancePolicy`, L73) | At least one assigned `macOSCompliancePolicy` has `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` in secured, low, medium **or high** (L72, L85). It fails when there is no macOS policy (L63-69). | **Don't name the step.** Learn documents the compliance risk score for Android, iOS/iPadOS and Windows only: overview.md L98-104, configure-integration.md L345 and L124-126 (no macOS toggle), deploy-compliance-step-3.md L202 and L253. The macOS settings reference has no such setting: `ref-macos-settings.md` has no "risk" or "threat" text, and the live page gives 0 matches. Graph has the property, but Learn documents no setting in the admin center. It also counts High, which blocks nothing (configure-integration.md L393-397) and which MT.1231 rejects. Separately, its guide describes a "Connect macOS devices" toggle and a macOS Defender section that Learn doesn't document, and it links to `https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/advanced-threat-protection`, which **returns 404**. Flag the test for review. |
207	| MT.1235 `Test.MT.1235.ps1` (helper L136) | At least one assigned **Android device administrator** `androidCompliancePolicy` has `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled = true` (L89-90). It fails with no Android policy (L72-78) and is Not applicable when only Android Enterprise policies exist (L80-87). | **A different setting.** `deviceThreatProtection*` is the third-party MTD "Device Threat Level" rule under Device Health (ref-android-administrator-settings.md L87; `mobile-threat-defense/create-compliance-policy.md` L69). It isn't the Defender "machine risk score" (L65-69, Graph `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel`). It also reads only device administrator, which Learn calls deprecated on GMS devices (configure-integration.md L74-76). Name **no step** in this goal. If a third-party MTD goal is added later, a step like `intune.compliance-mtd-threat-level` fits it. |
208	
209	## Other tests that read these settings
210	
211	Searches of `tests/` (all suites) and of the installed ZTA 3.1.0 tests:
212	
213	- **Not found in any suite:** `mobileThreatDefenseConnectors`, `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel`,
214	  `deviceThreatProtection`, `windows10CompliancePolicy`, EDR onboarding policies, or the Defender connector ID.
215	- **MT.1098, MT.1216, MT.1231, MT.1235:** the only hits; analysed in the table above.
216	- **No Windows machine-risk check, and no EDR-policy check**, in MT, CIS, CISA, ASD, EIDSCA, ORCA or ZTA.
217	- **EIDSCA and ORCA:** nothing relevant.
218	- **ZTA:** the only test that reads the connectors is ZTA.24871.
219	- **MT.1243 and MT.1249** read app protection `maximumAllowedDeviceThreatLevel` (iOS, Android). That is the
220	  app-protection branch (configure-integration.md L412-439), which is separate from compliance. They name no step
221	  here; a later `intune.app-protection-device-risk` step could hold them.
222	- **Defender AV checks (MT.1148-1171) and ZTA.24575, 24784, 41059, 41060:** antivirus settings, not part of this
223	  path.
224	
225	## ZTA IDs
226	
227	| ID | Title (catalog) | Step |
228	| --- | --- | --- |
